entries.title: Evaluator selections are kept when searching or changing plan filters
entries.summary: Checking an evaluator, then searching for another one, used to clear every earlier pick. Selections now survive a new search or plan-filter change; only switching events resets them. When some selected evaluators are not visible in the current search results, the selection bar shows **N not in this list** so the count is always clear before a bulk tag action.
entries.use_case: Events with hundreds of evaluators often need to find and tag several people across multiple searches. Organizers can now check evaluators one search at a time and bulk-apply tags to all of them in a single action without losing earlier picks.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer with a large evaluator pool (100+) reports that bulk-tagging evaluators is tedious because selections disappear between searches.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans with many evaluators who need to bulk-apply tags across multiple searches.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → Evaluators tab
internal.gotchas: The selection bar shows 'N not in this list' when selected evaluators are off the current page — reassure customers this is expected and those people are still included in the bulk request. Only switching events clears the selection; searching and plan-filter changes do not.
internal.talk_track: You can now search for evaluators one group at a time, check each one, and when you hit Edit Tags all your picks across every search are included — no need to tag them in separate passes.

draft.docs_gap: The Manage evaluators section should note that selections persist across searches and plan-filter changes, and explain the "N not in this list" indicator in the selection bar.
draft.why_use_it: null

entries.title: Bulk edit participant order across sessions
entries.summary: In **As submitted** mode, a new **Bulk edit order** page (from the **⋯** menu on a session's Participants list, or **More → Order participants** on selected sessions) sets one ordering rule — roles in the order you choose, then last name, first name, affiliation and more — previews which sessions would change, and reorders them all at once. Participants added later keep their submitted order until you apply the rules again.

enable.path: Program → Settings → Roles → Participant display order: As submitted

where.path: Session → Participants → ⋯ → Bulk edit order; Sessions → select → More → Order participants

entries.use_case: Programs that show participants as one list often still want a house style — moderators first, then speakers alphabetically. Instead of dragging each session by hand, organizers set the rule once and apply it to every session or a selection, with a preview first.

cs_action.note: Available wherever Participant Ordering Controls is on and the event uses As submitted.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer in As submitted mode asks to put moderators or chairs first, or to alphabetize speakers, across many sessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events already on Participant Ordering Controls with As submitted display order — typically medical/scientific programs and panels-heavy conferences.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → [session] → Participants → ⋯ → Bulk edit order
internal.gotchas: Applying is a one-time reorder, not a live sort: new participants land in submitted order until the rules are applied again. Not available in By role mode. Sessions already in order are skipped and not marked as updated.
internal.talk_track: Set the order once — roles in the order you want, then by last name — preview which sessions change, and reorder them all in one click.

entries.title: Control which attendee profile fields are editable in the Attend mobile app
entries.summary: A new **Attendee profile** section in the Attend app settings lets organizers choose which fields attendees can edit in the mobile app. **Photo**, **First name**, **Last name**, and **Email** are always shown, each with an **Editable** toggle (on by default). Use **Add a field** to include any other attendee field from the event; each added field can be toggled editable individually or removed with ✕. Fields the app cannot edit (such as rich text or file fields) appear read-only with an explanatory note.

enable.path: Event Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App → App Settings → Attendee profile

where.path: Attend → Mobile app → App Settings → Attendee profile

entries.use_case: Organizers who want attendees to keep their profiles accurate in the app — but need to lock down sensitive fields like email — can now choose exactly which fields are editable without any custom development. Events that collect additional attendee data (dietary needs, company, job title) can surface those fields in the app profile and let attendees self-serve updates.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the Attend Mobile App beta asks how attendees can update their own information, or when they want to prevent attendees from changing certain fields like email.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already on the Attend Mobile App beta who want to control attendee profile data in the app.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → Mobile app → App Settings → Attendee profile
internal.gotchas: The Attendee profile section only appears when the API returns a 'profile' key in settings — older API versions hide the section entirely and the PUT body omits the profile key, so there is no risk of breaking existing events on the old API. Email changes in the app require the attendee to confirm a code sent to the new address before the change takes effect.
internal.talk_track: You can now decide field by field what attendees can edit in their app profile — turn off Editable on Email to lock it down, or add your custom 'Dietary Preference' field so attendees can update it themselves without contacting your team.

draft.docs_gap: The Early Access guide does not document the Attend Mobile App settings panel or the Attendee profile section; a dedicated Attend Mobile App setup guide should cover how to configure app settings including attendee profile field visibility and editability.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend mobile app gives attendees a profile they carry through the event. Controlling which fields are editable lets you balance self-service convenience — attendees fix their own name or headshot — with data integrity, keeping fields like email or custom fields read-only when accuracy matters. You can extend the profile beyond the four core fields by adding any attendee field the event tracks, so the app profile reflects exactly what your program needs.

entries.title: Attendees can edit their profile, photo, and email address in the Attend app
entries.summary: Attendees using the Attend mobile app can now update their profile directly from the app: edit name and any organizer-enabled fields, upload or remove a profile photo (JPEG/PNG/WebP, up to 5 MB), and change their email address via a 6-digit verification code sent to the new address. Organizers control which fields are shown and whether each is editable via **App Settings → Profile**; field types the app cannot collect (rich text, files, lookups, date-times) are stored as read-only automatically.

where.path: Attend App → Profile (attendee-facing); Event Settings → App Settings → Profile (organizer-facing)

entries.use_case: Attendees no longer need to contact the event team to fix a typo in their name, swap their headshot, or update their email — they can do it themselves in the app. Organizers decide exactly which fields are editable, keeping sensitive or system-managed data locked while giving attendees autonomy over the rest.

cs_action.note: Organizers must configure which fields are shown/editable in App Settings → Profile. Defaults show all four core fields (photo, first name, last name, email) as editable. Worth confirming with customers that they are comfortable with attendees changing their own email address before the app goes live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the Attend app asks how attendees can self-serve profile corrections, or when they want to reduce inbound support requests about name/headshot/email changes.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running the Attend mobile app (beta) who wants attendees to manage their own profile data.
internal.gotchas: Email change sends a 6-digit code to the NEW address; the old address keeps working until verified. Five wrong codes revoke the change attempt. Old session tokens become invalid after a successful email change — the app issues new tokens automatically. A notice email to the old address is not included in this release (follow-up planned).
internal.talk_track: Attendees can now tap into their profile in the Attend app to fix their name, upload a headshot, or change their email — no need to contact your team. You control which fields they can edit from App Settings, so anything you want locked stays locked.

draft.docs_gap: The Attendee View guide (and ideally a dedicated Attend App profile guide) should document the App Settings → Profile configuration panel, the list of supported editable field types, the email-change verification flow, and the photo upload constraints (JPEG/PNG/WebP, 5 MB max).
draft.why_use_it: The Attend app gives attendees a personalised event experience on their phone. A complete, accurate profile helps other attendees and organizers identify and connect with the right people. Organizers choose which fields attendees can see and edit, so the profile stays consistent with event data while reducing support requests for simple corrections.

entries.title: App detail page now requires the same integrations permission as the Apps directory
entries.summary: The org-level app detail page (`/org/:orgId/apps/:appId`) was accessible to any org member who knew the URL, even without the **Integrations** read permission. It now applies the same access gate as the **Apps** directory: staff always pass, and all other users must hold the **Integrations** read permission to open the page or any of its tabs (connections, event mappings, sync, logs).
entries.use_case: Org admins who restrict integrations access to specific team members can now be confident that the app detail page — including connection credentials, event mappings, sync controls, and logs — is not reachable by anyone who lacks the Integrations read permission, even if they navigate directly to the URL.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that team members without integrations access were able to open app detail pages directly via URL.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer who restricts integrations visibility to a subset of org users.
internal.staff_path: Org → Apps → [any app] — confirm non-integrations users are blocked
internal.gotchas: Event-level 'Sync to …' and History cancel actions are unaffected — they use the event's 'Can manually sync records' permission, not org.integrations.read.
internal.talk_track: The app detail page now enforces the same permission as the Apps directory, so only team members you've granted integrations access to can view connection details, mappings, sync history, and logs.

draft.docs_gap: The App marketplace guide should note that both the Apps directory and individual app detail pages require the org-level Integrations read permission, and that event-level sync actions use a separate event permission.
draft.why_use_it: null

entries.title: Configure an attendee directory for the Attend mobile app
entries.summary: A new **Attendee directory** section in **Attend → Attendee App → Settings** lets organizers turn the in-app People directory on or off, choose whether attendees are listed by default or must opt in, and select which profile fields (photo, job title, company, registration type, bio, LinkedIn, website, email, phone) the directory displays. Name is always shown. Enabling **Email** or **Phone** displays a contact-details privacy warning.

enable.path: Attend → Attendee App → Settings → Attendee directory

where.path: Attend → Attendee App → Settings → Attendee directory

entries.use_case: Events that want to encourage networking can turn on the attendee directory so participants can browse and connect with each other in the Attend mobile app. Organizers control exactly which fields are visible and whether attendees are listed automatically or only when they choose to appear.

cs_action.note: The directory section only appears when the API supports it (PR #4523). Confirm the API is deployed for the customer's environment before walking them through the settings.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the Attend mobile app asks about networking features or wants attendees to be able to find each other in the app.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Attend beta who want to enable in-app attendee networking.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → Attendee App → Settings → Attendee directory
internal.gotchas: The Attendee directory section is hidden and no directory data is sent if the backend API (sessionboard-web-api#4523) has not been deployed for that environment. Verify API availability before demoing or enabling.
internal.talk_track: You can now give attendees a searchable directory right inside the Attend app. You control which fields show up and whether people are listed automatically or have to opt in — so you can match whatever privacy standard your event requires.

draft.docs_gap: The article index has no guide specifically covering Attend mobile app settings; the closest article (/marketing/attendee-view) covers a different surface. A dedicated guide for Attend → Attendee App → Settings should be created, documenting the Attendee directory toggle, the listed-by-default option, and the available directory fields including the email/phone privacy warning.
draft.why_use_it: The attendee directory in the Attend mobile app gives participants a searchable list of fellow attendees so they can find and connect with people before, during, and after the event. Organizers decide which profile fields are shown, keeping sensitive contact details like email and phone behind an explicit opt-in. The listing default — opt-in or opt-out — lets you match your event's privacy expectations without requiring manual configuration for every attendee.

entries.title: Attend app: speakers see their sessions and can post to LinkedIn
entries.summary: Attendees who are on the program now see a speaker profile in the Attend mobile app, showing every published session they are seated on (including legacy speaker, chair, and moderator roles). From that profile they can connect their LinkedIn account and post a branded share card — a 1200×627 image generated from the event's brand — directly to LinkedIn. The connection is per-registration and per-provider; a transferred registration never posts as the previous owner. The **Share** flow returns a signed card URL valid for 1 hour and lets the attendee edit the post text before publishing.

where.path: Attend app → My Profile → Speaker sessions / Share on LinkedIn

entries.use_case: Speakers at your event can open the Attend app, see their sessions, and share a branded LinkedIn post in seconds — driving awareness of your event and their participation without any extra tools or manual asset requests.

cs_action.note: LinkedIn posting requires LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID/SECRET and AMPLIFY_LINKEDIN_VAULT_KEY to be set in the environment (already done for dev and prod-us). The Attend app feature flag must be active. Confirm the companion mobile app PR (lennd/sessionboard-mobile) has also shipped before promoting this to customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the Attend app beta asks how speakers can promote their sessions or when they want to drive social buzz around their event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already on the Attend app beta who have speakers on a published program and want social amplification.
internal.staff_path: Attend app → speaker profile → Share on LinkedIn
internal.gotchas: The speaker UI is hidden in the app if the API version predates this release. LinkedIn posting uses the existing /creator/linkedin/callback redirect URI — no LinkedIn app changes needed. Seats hidden from the public roster still appear to the speaker in the app. Draft or deleted sessions are excluded.
internal.talk_track: Speakers open the Attend app, tap their session, and hit Share — they get a polished branded card posted to LinkedIn in under a minute, with no asset requests to your team.

draft.docs_gap: The Attendee view guide should document the new speaker profile section in the Attend app, the LinkedIn connect flow, and the branded share card, including how sessions are matched and what happens when a registration is transferred.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend app gives every registered attendee a personalised event companion on their phone. Speakers get a dedicated view of their sessions and a one-tap path to share their participation on LinkedIn with a branded card, helping them promote the event to their professional network. The connection is tied to their registration so it works securely across devices and survives registration transfers.

entries.title: Sponsor and exhibitor staff see their team in the Attend app
entries.summary: Sponsor and exhibitor contacts who are registered for an event now appear in the **Partners** section of their Attend app profile. A new team endpoint lets them view fellow booth staff — name, job title, photo, and role — for any partner organisation they belong to. Members of other events, other organisations, or deleted accounts are never shown.
entries.use_case: Exhibitor and sponsor staff attending an event can open the Attend app and immediately see who else from their company is on-site, along with each person's role and job title — useful for coordinating booth coverage without exchanging contact details manually.

cs_action.note: This is the API half only; the companion mobile app PR (lennd/sessionboard-mobile) must also ship before the feature is visible to end users. Confirm both are released before promoting.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with sponsors or exhibitors asks how booth staff will use the Attend app at their event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Attend app (beta) who also have sponsors or exhibitors set up on their event.
internal.gotchas: The partners list only appears once the companion mobile app PR ships. A contact is matched to a sponsor/exhibitor team via Account_Contacts or by email match (case-insensitive); contacts from other events in the same org or other orgs sharing the same email are explicitly excluded. Team member list is capped at 200 and excludes cancelled registrations and the viewer themselves. Photos rejected by moderation show as null.
internal.talk_track: Sponsor and exhibitor staff open the Attend app and see their company listed under Partners. Tapping it shows the rest of the booth team — name, title, photo and role — so everyone knows who's representing the company on the floor.

draft.docs_gap: The Attend app guide should document the Partners section of the profile screen, explain how a contact is matched to a sponsor or exhibitor team, and note the 200-member cap and the team-member visibility rules.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend mobile app gives every registered attendee a personalised event experience in their pocket. Sponsor and exhibitor contacts get a dedicated Partners view that surfaces their organisation's profile and booth team, so staff can coordinate on the floor without needing a separate directory or group chat. The team list is scoped strictly to the current event, keeping information relevant and secure.

entries.title: Attend app: browse and search a live attendee directory
entries.summary: The Attend mobile app now includes an **Attendees** directory under **People**. Organizers enable the directory in app settings and choose which profile fields (**Photo**, **Job Title**, **Company**, **Bio**, **LinkedIn**, **Website**, **Email**, **Phone**, **Registrant Type**) are shown; email and phone are hidden unless explicitly ticked. Attendees opt in or out of being listed, and can override the event default at any time. The directory lists only live, confirmed or checked-in registrants who have not withdrawn consent, sorted A–Z by last name with a side-index letter jump, keyword search, company filter, registrant-type filter, and keyset cursor pagination. When a registration is transferred, the previous holder's opt-in status and personal field values are cleared automatically.

enable.path: Event App Settings → Directory → Enable Attendees Directory

entries.use_case: Events that want to foster networking can let attendees discover and connect with each other directly in the Attend app. Organizers control exactly which fields are visible and the directory only surfaces attendees who have actively opted in, keeping personal data protected.

cs_action.note: Directory is off by default and nobody is listed by default; organizer must turn it on in Event App Settings and choose which fields to expose before attendees see anything.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the Attend app asks about in-app networking or attendee discovery features.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already on the Attend app beta who run networking-focused events and want attendees to find each other without a separate app.
internal.gotchas: Email and phone are never shown unless the organizer explicitly ticks those fields. Registration transfers automatically clear the previous holder's opt-in and personal field values — reassure customers this is intentional for privacy. The directory returns 403 with code directory_off when the feature is disabled, so integrations or deep links will surface that error if the setting is toggled off mid-event.
internal.talk_track: With the attendee directory, your participants can search for colleagues, filter by company or registration type, and browse alphabetically — all inside the Attend app. You decide which fields are public, and every attendee chooses whether they appear at all.

draft.docs_gap: The /marketing/attendee-view guide covers the web-based attendee view but does not document the Attend app's in-app attendee directory, its admin settings (fields, default listing, opt-in flow), privacy rules, or the A–Z cursor-paginated search and filter experience — all of these should be added.
draft.why_use_it: The attendee directory gives event participants a way to find and learn about fellow attendees without leaving the Attend app. You control which profile fields are shown, set a default listing preference, and attendees can always choose whether they appear. The directory respects consent state and registration status, so only live, opted-in attendees are ever visible.

entries.title: Org members with integrations read permission can now see the event Apps sidebar item
entries.summary: The **Apps** row in the event sidebar (`/event/:id/apps`) was previously visible only to Sessionboard staff. Org members who hold the **org.integrations.read** permission on the event's organization now see **Apps** in the event sidebar alongside staff. Users without that org permission — including event-only users — continue to see no **Apps** row.
entries.use_case: Organizations that delegate integration management to specific team members — such as a technical ops lead — can now grant those people the integrations read permission so they see and access the event Apps section directly, without needing staff-level access.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that a non-staff team member cannot see the Apps section in the event sidebar despite being responsible for managing integrations.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the new navigation (nav_v2) who have org members managing integrations who previously had to rely on staff to access event Apps.
internal.gotchas: This only applies when the event's org has new_navigation (nav_v2) enabled. Event-only users — those without an org-level role — will never see the Apps row regardless of any event permission they hold.
internal.talk_track: If you have a team member who manages your integrations, you can now give them the org integrations read permission and they will see the Apps section in the event sidebar just like staff do — no need to escalate to us for every sync.

draft.docs_gap: The sidebar guide should note that the event Apps row is visible to org members with the org.integrations.read permission (in addition to staff), and that event-only users cannot see it.
draft.why_use_it: The event sidebar's Apps section gives organizers quick access to all integration connections and sync controls for an event. Controlling visibility through the org-level integrations permission means you can give the right team members access to manage third-party connections without opening up broader admin capabilities.

entries.title: Attend app layout templates: packs, page templates, home blocks and theme settings
entries.summary: Organizers can now configure the visual layout of the Attend mobile app from event app settings. Choose from 7 **Layout Packs** (e.g. Atlas), set page templates, home screen blocks, navigation style, corner radius, density and color scheme. The selected layout is bundled with the app so it loads correctly even when attendees are offline.

where.path: Event App → Settings → App Design → Layout

entries.use_case: Events with distinct brand identities can now match the Attend app's look and feel to their conference theme — choosing a layout pack, home blocks and color scheme — without custom development. The layout is cached in the app bundle so attendees see the correct design even without a network connection.

cs_action.note: The admin 'App Design' UI (web-ui-v2) and the mobile resolver/Atlas templates ship in separate follow-on PRs. The API is live but the organizer-facing settings screen is not yet available. Do not proactively announce to customers until the web-ui-v2 PR ships.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the Attend mobile app beta asks about customising the app's appearance or branding.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already on the Attend mobile app beta who want to align the app's visual design with their event brand.
internal.staff_path: Event → App Settings → Layout (available once web-ui-v2 ships)
internal.gotchas: The API endpoint is live but the organizer UI ('App Design' screen) and mobile resolver/Atlas templates are in separate follow-on PRs — customers cannot yet configure this from the product UI. Default layout is Atlas pack with large radius, comfortable density and auto color scheme.
internal.talk_track: You will soon be able to pick a layout pack and home screen blocks for your Attend app right from event settings, and the design will be cached so it works offline for your attendees.

draft.docs_gap: No guide currently covers the Attend mobile app layout/design settings. A new article (or a section in an Attend app guide) should document the available layout packs, page templates, home blocks, nav styles, theme options and how the layout is bundled for offline use.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend mobile app layout system lets you control how your event looks and feels for every attendee on their phone. Pick a layout pack that matches your brand, choose which blocks appear on the home screen, and set the color scheme, density and corner style — all from event settings. Because the layout ships inside the app bundle, attendees get a consistent experience whether they are online or offline.

entries.title: Mobile App settings move to Publish → Mobile App, with a new org-level roll-up and app editor
entries.summary: **Mobile App** settings have moved from **Attend** into **Publish → Mobile App** at both the event and organization level. At the event level, the same app settings panel is now found under **Publish → Mobile App**; the old **Attend → Mobile App** path redirects there automatically. At the org level, a new **Mobile App** page shows a roll-up of every event's app (dates, status, sign-in methods, layout pack, and a direct link to each event's settings), plus an organization app editor — gated by the **attend_org_app** Early Access feature — where organizers can configure the org app's name, tagline, logo, colours, featured events, Media library picks, and info pages.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → attend_app (event); org app editor requires attend_org_app Early Access

entries.use_case: Organizers managing multiple events can now see every event's mobile app status in one place at the org level, and — when the org app feature is enabled — configure a single branded organization app covering all their events without jumping between event settings pages.

cs_action.note: The org-level app editor (attend_org_app) requires a separate Early Access flag beyond attend_app. Confirm with the customer which flag(s) they need before enabling.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks where Mobile App settings went, or when a multi-event customer wants a single branded app across their portfolio.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already on the Attend Mobile App beta who manage multiple events and want a unified org-level app experience.
internal.staff_path: Org → Publish → Mobile App; Event → Publish → Mobile App
internal.gotchas: The old Attend → Mobile App route redirects automatically. The org app editor only appears when the attend_org_app Early Access flag is on. If the API hasn't shipped (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4528), the sidebar rows may not appear and the org editor shows an 'isn't available on this server yet' message — no retries, no error loop.
internal.talk_track: Mobile App settings now live under Publish → Mobile App at both the event and org level. At the org level you get a dashboard of every event's app, and if you're on the org app preview you can build one app that covers all your events — name, branding, featured content, and info pages — all in one place.

draft.docs_gap: The Early Access guide should document the attend_app and attend_org_app feature flags, explain the new Publish → Mobile App location at both event and org scope, and describe the org-level roll-up table and org app editor fields (name, tagline, logo, colours, events selection, featured order, Media picks, info pages).
draft.why_use_it: The Mobile App settings surface gives organizers a single destination to configure and publish their event's attendee app. At the organization level, the roll-up view lets teams track app status across every event at a glance, while the org app editor lets you build one branded app that spans multiple events, complete with featured sessions, media, and custom info pages.

entries.title: Attend app: share content as a sponsor or exhibitor company, and team lists respect attendee directory preferences
entries.summary: Two related improvements to the Attend mobile app for partner (sponsor/exhibitor) teams. First, attendees who are on a sponsor or exhibitor team can now share event content on LinkedIn as their company rather than as themselves — the share card shows the company name, sponsor tier, booth location, and the attendee's name. Second, the team member list now respects each attendee's directory opt-out and consent settings: attendees who have opted out of the directory or withdrawn consent are hidden from the team list, and **Job Title** and **Photo** only appear for teammates whose directory profile includes those fields.

where.path: Attend mobile app → Share → Share as [Company]

entries.use_case: Sponsors and exhibitors want their company brand — not just individual employees — amplified on LinkedIn during an event. Attendees on a partner team can now post as their company with the correct tier label and booth details automatically included, while the team roster stays clean by hiding colleagues who have opted out of the attendee directory.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a sponsor or exhibitor asks how their booth staff can promote the event on LinkedIn as the company rather than as individuals, or when a partner reports seeing unexpected colleagues in their team list.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Attend app (beta) who have sponsors or exhibitors with multiple staff members attending the event.
internal.staff_path: Attend mobile app → partner team view → Share button
internal.gotchas: The 'share as company' option only appears if the attendee is a confirmed member of that partner team (same access rule as the /me partners endpoint). Booth location on the share card is pulled from published floor maps only — unpublished maps will not show booth numbers. Job title and photo are suppressed for teammates who have not included those fields in their directory profile, even if the data exists on their contact record.
internal.talk_track: Your booth staff can now tap Share in the Attend app and choose to post as your company on LinkedIn — the card automatically pulls in your sponsor tier and booth number. And the team list only shows colleagues who have opted into the attendee directory, so everyone's privacy choices are respected.

draft.docs_gap: The Advocacy guide covers speaker and attendee sharing but does not document the partner/company actor type in the Attend app; it should add a section explaining how sponsor and exhibitor team members can share as their company, what appears on the share card (tier, booth, company name), and how directory opt-out affects the team member list.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend mobile app gives sponsors, exhibitors, and attendees a way to share event content and connect with colleagues directly from their phones. Partner teams let a company's booth staff coordinate and share as a unified presence, reinforcing brand visibility across social channels without requiring manual setup for each individual. Directory-aware team lists ensure that only people who have consented to be visible appear to their colleagues, keeping privacy preferences consistent across the app.

entries.title: Org members with integrations read permission can now access event Apps pages
entries.summary: The event **Apps** pages (the marketplace list and individual app detail pages) were previously restricted to staff. Org members who hold the **org.integrations: read** permission on the event's organization can now open these pages; members without the permission see the standard permission-denied screen.
entries.use_case: Organizations that delegate integration management to a dedicated ops or tech team can now grant those members the org-level integrations read permission so they can browse and configure event app connections without needing staff access.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why their integration manager or tech lead cannot see the Apps section in an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer whose integration work is handled by a non-staff org member rather than a Sessionboard admin.
internal.gotchas: The permission is org-scoped (org.integrations: read), not event-scoped. The event sidebar Apps row also requires the same permission to appear, gated by the paired API change in sessionboard-web-api#4530.
internal.talk_track: If your integration team isn't staff, you can now give them the org integrations read permission and they'll see the Apps section in every event — no need to involve a Sessionboard admin for day-to-day integration work.

draft.docs_gap: The App Marketplace guide should note that org members with the org.integrations: read permission can access event Apps pages, and explain how to grant that permission via org team settings.
draft.why_use_it: The App Marketplace lets you connect Sessionboard to your registration platform, networking tools, and other event technology so that session and speaker data flows automatically between systems. Granting the right team members access to the Apps pages means the people responsible for integrations can manage connections directly, without routing every request through a staff administrator.

entries.title: Attend app correctly blocks access to deleted or archived events and archived organizations
entries.summary: Attendees who open the **Attend** mobile app for a deleted event now receive a clear "not found" response instead of being served live data. Archived events return a **EVENT_ARCHIVED** error and archived organizations return an **ORGANIZATION_ARCHIVED** error, so the app can display a "no longer available" message. Existing attendee sessions (tokens) for deleted or archived events also expire on the next refresh, ending access cleanly.
entries.use_case: When an organizer deletes or archives an event, attendees who still have the Attend app open are now blocked from viewing any event data — auth, schedule, files, moments, credits, and more — rather than continuing to access a live feed of a gone event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks what happens to attendees in the Attend app when they archive or delete an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Attend mobile app beta.
internal.gotchas: Previously valid attendee tokens for deleted/archived events will 401 on the next refresh — attendees will be signed out automatically. This is intentional. The error codes EVENT_ARCHIVED and ORGANIZATION_ARCHIVED are returned to the app so it can show a user-friendly 'no longer available' screen rather than a generic error.
internal.talk_track: If you archive or delete an event, attendees in the Attend app are immediately blocked — they see a clear 'no longer available' message rather than stale or live data from a closed event.

draft.docs_gap: The Attendee view guide should note what attendees experience in the Attend app when an event is deleted or archived, including that existing sessions expire and a "no longer available" message is shown.
draft.why_use_it: null

entries.title: Attendees can save sessions, speakers, sponsors, exhibitors, people, topics, tracks, rooms and files in the Attend app
entries.summary: Attendees using the Attend mobile app can now **Save** any session, speaker, sponsor, exhibitor, fellow attendee, topic tag, track, room or session file. Saved sessions form the attendee's **My schedule** — a personal agenda built from the event programme. A **Save** / **Saved** toggle (bookmark icon) appears on each item; saves sync across devices and work offline, with the most-recent action always winning. Saving a session also feeds the existing recommendations engine, so the app's suggested sessions reflect what the attendee has bookmarked.

where.path: Attend mobile app → any session, speaker, sponsor, exhibitor, person, topic, track, room or file detail

Admin counts ('saved by N attendees') are not yet surfaced — that is a planned follow-up.
internal.talk_track: Attendees can tap the bookmark on any session, speaker, sponsor or exhibitor to save it. Their saved sessions become their My schedule — a personal agenda that syncs across every device they use, even if they were offline when they tapped Save.

draft.docs_gap: The Attendee view guide should be updated (or a new Attend app guide created) to document the Save / Saved bookmark interaction, the My schedule concept, cross-device sync behaviour, and the offline queue — none of which are currently covered.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend mobile app gives event attendees a personalised view of the programme in their pocket. Saves let attendees curate their own schedule and reference list from the full event catalogue — sessions, speakers, sponsors, exhibitors, fellow attendees, topics, tracks, rooms and files — without any organiser intervention. Saved sessions feed the app's recommendation engine, so the more an attendee saves, the more relevant their suggested content becomes. Saves sync across devices in real time and queue reliably when the attendee is offline.

entries.title: Venue Maps settings in the mobile app: link zones to session rooms, new wayfinding POI types, and a map list

enable.path: Publish → Mobile App → Venue Maps

where.path: Publish → Mobile App → Venue Maps; Floor Maps designer → Zone inspector / POI palette

entries.use_case: Events with complex venues can now tie each floor-map zone directly to a session room so the app and printed program stay in sync, and can surface precise wayfinding points — elevators, first-aid stations, charging spots, and more — so attendees always know where to go. The curated map list gives organizers full control over which maps appear in the attendee app and in what order.

A new guide should document: linking a zone to a session room, the full list of POI kinds and how to place them, and how to configure the Maps in the app list (adding Sessionboard floor maps, ExpoFP plans, and HTTPS links; reordering; publishing/unpublishing).
draft.why_use_it: Floor Maps lets you draw interactive venue maps that appear in the Attend mobile app and in printed program books. Linking zones to session rooms keeps your agenda and your map consistent without double-entry, while the expanded POI palette gives attendees the wayfinding detail they need to navigate a large or multi-level venue. The Venue Maps settings panel gives you one place to decide which maps attendees see, in what order, and whether each map is published or still a draft.

entries.title: Attend app: add any session to your calendar and subscribe to your personal schedule feed
entries.summary: Attendees in the Attend mobile app can now tap **Add to Calendar** on any session to download a `.ics` file that opens directly in Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, Outlook, or any other calendar app. A personal **My Schedule** feed URL (subscribable via `webcal://`) keeps saved sessions up to date automatically — if an organizer moves a session, the change appears on the next hourly refresh. Tapping **Reset feed link** invalidates the old URL and issues a new one.

The subscribable My Schedule feed is especially useful at multi-day conferences where the program can shift — saved sessions stay accurate without the attendee doing anything.

The My Schedule feed stops working if a registration is cancelled or transferred; the attendee must use the new link after a reset. The mobile UI PR is separate (sessionboard-mobile); this entry covers the API half only — hold publication until the app side ships.

The personal schedule feed updates automatically, so a last-minute room change or time shift reaches every subscriber without a manual re-download.

entries.title: Report builder gains "Every value, in one cell" and "Spread (standard deviation)" calculations
entries.summary: Two new aggregate calculations are available in the report builder's calculation menu. **Every value, in one cell** (LIST) works on text and number columns and displays all individual values together — for example, each reviewer's score or comment for a submission. **Spread (standard deviation)** uses population standard deviation (equivalent to Excel's STDEV.P) and works on number columns.
entries.use_case: Events using scored evaluations can now pull every reviewer's individual score into a single cell alongside the average, making it easy to spot outliers at a glance. The standard deviation calculation lets program teams quantify how much reviewer opinions diverged on any numeric field without leaving the report builder.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to see all individual reviewer scores side-by-side, or wants to measure scoring consistency across reviewers.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running scored evaluation plans who want to analyse reviewer agreement or surface raw scores in a report.
internal.staff_path: Event → Reporting → Reports → open or create a report → add a column → set Calculation
internal.gotchas: The API (sessionboard-web-api#4535) must be deployed before these calculations return results; without it the engine rejects LIST and STDDEV_POP. Confirm the API deploy is live before demoing.
internal.talk_track: You can now add a column to any report that shows every reviewer's score in one cell — great for spotting when one reviewer rated a session very differently from the rest. The standard deviation column gives you a single number that tells you how spread out the scores were, without needing to export to Excel.

draft.docs_gap: The Build a report guide should document the full list of available calculation types — including LIST (Every value, in one cell) and STDDEV_POP (Spread / standard deviation) — with a note on which column data types each calculation supports.
draft.why_use_it: The report builder lets you query, group, and aggregate session and speaker data without exporting to a spreadsheet. Use it when you need a live, shareable view of evaluation scores, submission counts, or any numeric field — with calculations like sum, average, and now spread and full value lists available directly in the tool.

entries.title: New Attend module for the attendee mobile app admin

entries.title: Report builder gains LIST, STDDEV_POP, and label-keyed rubric fields for reviewer score sheets
entries.summary: Three new capabilities are available when building SbQL reports on review data. **LIST(field)** collects every reviewer's value for a submission into one cell (numbers joined with `, `, text with ` | `). **STDDEV_POP(field)** computes the population standard deviation across reviewers, returning blank when fewer than two values exist. **reviews_v2.rubric_label_\<slug\>** and **reviews_v2.rubric_label_\<slug\>_score** address a rubric question by its label across all evaluation plans and rounds, so a single query can span events with many plans. A row-cap bug that caused submissions beyond the first 10 000 assignments to return blank IDs and titles is also fixed.
entries.use_case: Events with many evaluation plans — such as a conference running 25 per-category review rounds — can now build a single final score sheet that shows each reviewer's individual scores, internal comments, and population standard deviation in one row per submission, sorted by average score, without writing custom SQL or exporting to Excel.

cs_action.note: Customers running large multi-plan reviews (25+ plans, 10k+ assignments) were silently getting blank session IDs on roughly 40% of rows before the row-cap fix. Proactively flag this fix to any customer who reported missing data in SbQL review reports.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to produce a final score sheet with per-reviewer scores and spread statistics, or when they have multiple evaluation plans and need a single cross-plan report.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans, especially those with many plans or rounds (medical conferences, large CFP programs) who need statistical summaries of reviewer scores.
internal.staff_path: Event → Reporting → Reports → New Report → SbQL
internal.gotchas: LIST returns text, so it cannot be used inside a HAVING clause. STDDEV_POP returns blank (not zero) when fewer than two non-blank values exist for a group. Label-keyed rubric fields (rubric_label_<slug>) match by the question label set in the plan, so the label must be consistent across plans for cross-plan queries to work.
internal.talk_track: You can now write one report query that pulls every reviewer's score and comments into a single row per submission, calculates the spread with STDDEV_POP, and sorts by average — covering all your evaluation plans at once, with no Excel gymnastics required.

draft.docs_gap: The Build a report guide should document the LIST and STDDEV_POP aggregate functions, the reviews_v2.rubric_label_<slug> and reviews_v2.rubric_label_<slug>_score field syntax, and include an example score-sheet query showing GROUP BY with COMPUTE clauses.
draft.why_use_it: The report builder lets you query submission and reviewer data using SbQL, a structured query language designed for Sessionboard's evaluation model. You can group results by session, aggregate scores across reviewers, and sort or filter the output — all without leaving the platform. It is the fastest way to produce a final score sheet, identify outlier scores, or share ranked results with a program committee.

entries.title: Upload a venue PDF as a hall background in Floor Maps
entries.summary: Organizers can now upload a venue PDF directly as a hall background instead of manually exporting it to PNG or SVG first. In the Floor Maps designer, select a hall, choose **Upload PDF**, provide the PDF URL and the page number to render, and Sessionboard converts the chosen page to a high-resolution image (up to 4096 px on the long edge) and sets it as the hall background automatically.
entries.use_case: Medical and association venues typically supply floor plans as PDFs. Organizers can now point Sessionboard at the PDF and pick the page they need — no manual image conversion required — cutting a common onboarding bottleneck for Attend venue maps.

cs_action.note: Feature is staff-gated on the UI side (web-ui-v2#1021) until both PRs ship together. Confirm the UI gate is lifted before telling customers this is available.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using Floor Maps / Attend says they received a multi-page PDF from their venue and are struggling to get it into the hall background.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Floor Maps beta, especially medical, association, or convention-centre events where venues supply PDF floor plans.
internal.gotchas: PDF must be hosted on a trusted CDN (Filestack or the content CDN); direct links to arbitrary URLs are rejected. File cap is 50 MB and max 200 pages. If the hall background changes while the render job is running, the job preserves the newer background and reports a failure — reassure the organizer this is intentional.
internal.talk_track: If your venue hands you a PDF, just paste the link into Floor Maps, pick the page, and Sessionboard renders it at full resolution as your hall background — no Photoshop, no export step.

draft.docs_gap: The Floor Maps / Attend guide should document the PDF background upload flow: where to find it in the hall editor, supported PDF sources (Filestack / content CDN), the page-selection step, the async rendering job and its status states (pending, rendering, done, failed), the 50 MB / 200-page limits, and what happens if the background changes while a render is in progress.
draft.why_use_it: Floor Maps lets you design the spatial layout of your venue inside Sessionboard and publish it to the Attend mobile app so attendees can navigate the event. Uploading a PDF background means you can use the official venue floor plan exactly as supplied, choose the specific page that matches each hall, and keep your map accurate without any image-editing tools.

entries.title: Scholar template pack for the mobile app — agenda options, button filters, and new destinations
entries.summary: The **Scholar** template pack is now available in **Publish → Mobile App → App design**, pre-configured for medical and scientific conferences with a dense 3-across session grid, faculty list, and a **Home · Program · Search · Credits · Me** toolbar. When the agenda uses the **Browse by facets** layout, a new **Agenda options** block lets organizers choose which browsing dimensions to expose (Day, Track, Topic, Session type, Learning level, Speaker, Session code) and toggle **Show session codes** and **Show credits**. Home-screen buttons that open the agenda can now be filtered to a specific facet value (e.g. a button labelled "Committee meetings" that opens the agenda pre-filtered to Session type "Committee meeting"). Tab and button targets gain **Map**, **Search**, **Slides**, **My notes**, **Posters**, and **Abstracts** as destinations.
entries.use_case: Medical societies and scientific associations running poster-heavy or abstract-driven conferences can pick the Scholar pack and immediately get a layout tuned for their audience — dense session grids, faculty lists, credits display, and session codes — without building the design from scratch. The new agenda options and button filters let organizers surface exactly the right browsing paths (e.g. a one-tap "Posters" button filtered to the Poster session type) so attendees reach relevant content faster.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a medical society, scientific association, or CME-accredited conference customer asks about the mobile app or mentions needing poster/abstract browsing and credits display.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running medical, scientific, or academic conferences with abstracts, posters, faculty lists, or continuing-education credits who are on the Attend beta.
internal.staff_path: Event → Publish → Mobile App → App design → Pack picker → Scholar
internal.gotchas: Agenda options and button filters are hidden on older API versions (pre-release of web-api#4538) — they will appear automatically once that API release ships with no UI change needed. Resetting a page to pack defaults clears any custom agenda options.
internal.talk_track: If your attendees need to browse posters, find faculty, or track CME credits, the Scholar pack sets all of that up in one click. You can then fine-tune which browsing dimensions appear in the agenda and add shortcut buttons that drop attendees straight into a filtered session list — like a one-tap 'Posters' button.

draft.docs_gap: No guide currently documents the Attend mobile app's App design editor, Scholar pack, agenda options block, or button filter capability — a dedicated article covering pack selection, agenda options, and home-button filters should be created under the Apps or Attend section.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend mobile app's App design editor lets organizers choose a template pack that sets the visual style, navigation tabs, and home-screen buttons for their attendee app. Packs give a consistent starting point that can be adjusted per event, and the phone preview shows exactly what attendees will see before anything is published. The Scholar pack is designed for conferences where attendees need quick access to abstracts, posters, faculty, and continuing-education credits.

entries.title: Attend app: send push notifications to attendees and surface personalised recommendations

internal.talk_track: You can now send a targeted push to, say, everyone who saved a particular track to let them know the room changed — or mark it Urgent to guarantee it cuts through quiet hours. Meanwhile every attendee's home screen shows a Recommended block tailored to their interests, so they spend less time scrolling and more time at sessions they actually care about.

draft.docs_gap: The Attendee view guide should add sections covering: (1) how organizers create, segment, schedule, and send push notifications including the test-send and Urgent options; (2) how the Recommendations feature works, including the interests onboarding step, the ranking signals (saved content, declared interests, popularity), and the admin controls for pins/boosts/hides.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend mobile app puts your event program in every attendee's pocket. Push notifications let you reach the right segment of attendees instantly — whether that's everyone, speakers, or people who saved a particular track — and the personalised Recommended block surfaces sessions and exhibitors each attendee is most likely to care about based on their declared interests and saved content. Together they reduce the effort attendees spend hunting for what to do next and give organizers a direct, measurable channel to drive on-site engagement.

entries.title: Posters & abstracts are now available in the Attend app
entries.summary: The Attend mobile and web app gains a **Posters & Abstracts** section. Attendees can browse a paginated index of poster boards — including title, board number, track, topics, room, time, and author names — and tap into any item to read the full abstract (HTML), view author details with headshots, and download or preview the poster file. Signed, time-limited poster file links are generated on demand. Embargo rules (none, until-presentation, or fixed date) are honoured across the index, detail view, poster file links, and the offline bundle. The bundle also no longer incorrectly surfaces abstract submissions or withdrawn sessions as agenda items.

enable.path: Event Settings → Attend App → Posters & Abstracts → Enable

entries.use_case: Medical and scientific events with hundreds or thousands of poster submissions can now surface ePosters and abstracts directly in the Attend app, letting attendees browse boards, read full abstracts, and download poster files — all with embargo controls so content stays hidden until the right moment.

cs_action.note: The Posters & Abstracts section must be enabled in Attend App settings and configured to point at Poster Galleries, poster-session formats, or accepted abstracts. Mobile and web-ui-v2 PRs are required before attendees see the UI.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When talking to medical, scientific, or academic event customers (Cadmium / Sherpa ICP) who use ePosters or abstract submissions and are on the Attend app beta.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with Poster Galleries or poster-session formats and a large abstract corpus; requires the Attend app beta to be active.
internal.staff_path: Event Settings → Attend App → Posters & Abstracts
internal.gotchas: This PR is the API half only — the mobile and web-ui-v2 UI PRs must also ship before attendees see anything. Embargo is enforced across the index, detail, file links, and the bundle; gallery-level 'hide' and 'teaser' modes are also respected. The bundle fix (abstract submissions and withdrawn sessions no longer appear as agenda sessions) changes digests for affected events even without the posters feature enabled.
internal.talk_track: If your event has hundreds of poster boards or accepted abstracts, the Attend app can now show attendees a searchable poster index with full abstract text, author headshots, and downloadable poster files — and you control exactly when each piece of content becomes visible with embargo settings.

draft.docs_gap: The Poster galleries guide should add a section explaining how to configure the Attend app's Posters & Abstracts section, including source options (Poster Galleries, poster-session formats, accepted abstracts), embargo modes, board-number-to-map-booth linking, and how signed poster file links work.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend app's Posters & Abstracts section gives attendees a single place to discover, read, and download poster content at medical and scientific conferences. Embargo settings ensure abstract text, poster files, and author details are withheld until a session begins or a fixed date passes. Poster boards link to floor-map booth locations so attendees can navigate directly to a presenter. The offline-capable index means attendees can browse thousands of posters even with limited connectivity on the show floor.

entries.title: Mobile App settings replaced by a WYSIWYG editor with draft → publish
entries.summary: The **Publish → Mobile App** page for both event and org apps is now a full WYSIWYG editor modelled on the Site builder. A live phone preview renders the event's real program content; a left-hand page list covers Home, Agenda, Session, People, Partners, Map, Me, Design (Layout, Theme, Tabs), and Access; and a right-hand inspector lets organizers add, reorder, show/hide, and remove home blocks. Every layout and venue-map change autosaves to a draft — attendees see nothing until **Publish** is clicked. A **Draft saved / Unpublished changes / Live** status pill, undo/redo (⌘Z), **Discard**, and an **App on / App off** badge sit in the top bar. Access settings (app on/off, sign-in methods, SSO, attendee profile, directory) save instantly and are labelled **Saves at once — not part of the draft**. The org app editor adds a canvas of the org home (branding header, featured events, event list, media, info pages) with the same draft/publish flow.
entries.use_case: Organizers who manage a mobile app can now see exactly how their home screen looks — with real session and speaker data — before pushing any change live. The draft/publish model means the team can iterate on layout, theme, and blocks without attendees seeing work in progress.

cs_action.note: The editor only activates when the API returns a revision field (web-api #4541 must be deployed). Until both PRs are live in prod the old forms render unchanged — confirm both are deployed before demoing.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the Attend Mobile App asks how to customise their app home screen, change the layout pack, or manage what attendees see before an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer on the Attend Mobile App beta who wants visual control over their app's home screen, layout, and branding without waiting for support.
internal.staff_path: Event → Publish → Mobile App (or Org → Publish → Mobile App with attend_org_app on)
internal.gotchas: Access settings (app on/off, SSO, sign-in methods, directory) save instantly and bypass the draft — remind customers these changes are live immediately. The editor requires the API draft endpoint (web-api #4541); against an older API the old forms still render. Org app layout template selection requires a separate Attend app update not yet shipped.
internal.talk_track: You can now design your mobile app home screen visually — pick a layout pack, drag blocks around, preview it on a phone with your real sessions — and nothing goes live until you hit Publish. Security settings like sign-in methods still save instantly so you're never blocked on access controls.

draft.docs_gap: The /site/site-builder guide documents the Site builder; a dedicated Mobile App editor guide (referenced in the PR as sessionboard-docs #31) is needed to cover the draft/publish flow, what saves instantly vs. as a draft, the layout packs, block types, org app canvas, and the phone preview.
draft.why_use_it: The Mobile App editor gives organizers a visual, phone-shaped canvas to design and preview their attendee app without touching any code. Changes to layout, blocks, theme, and venue maps are held in a draft until the organizer is ready to publish, so attendees always see a polished, intentional experience. Security and access settings — such as sign-in methods and directory visibility — save immediately so privacy controls are never delayed by the draft cycle. The editor works for both per-event apps and the organization-level app from a single, consistent interface.

entries.title: Attend app: exhibitor showrooms, products, and Expo/Pulse layout packs
entries.summary: Exhibitors and sponsors in the Attend mobile app now have a **Showroom** page — including tagline, categories, photo gallery, public contacts, deals, video link, and label/value facts — and up to 100 **Products** per account (name, category, description, up to 8 photos). Organizers manage showrooms via **Event Settings → Attend → Showrooms**. Two new app layout packs are available: **Expo** (grid home, exhibitor directory, agenda with day tabs, and a Scan tab) and **Pulse** (personal feed home, timeline agenda, promoted partners carousel, floating-pill navigation).

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the Attend app; then Event Settings → Attend → Showrooms

entries.use_case: Events with trade show floors or sponsor tiers can give each exhibitor a rich, Map Your Show-style page inside the Attend app — complete with products, deals, and a photo gallery — so attendees can research and save exhibitors before and during the event. The Expo and Pulse layout packs let organizers match the app's navigation to the character of their event without custom configuration.

cs_action.note: This is the web-api half only; the admin UI (web-ui-v2) and mobile client ship separately. Do not surface to customers until all three parts are live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running a trade show or expo asks how exhibitors can have a richer presence in the Attend app, or when they want a pre-configured app layout for a specific event type.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already on the Attend beta who have exhibitors or sponsors and want to offer a directory-style showroom experience in the mobile app.

Writes require EVENT.SETTINGS.UPDATE permission.
internal.talk_track: With Showrooms, every exhibitor gets their own page in your event app — products, deals, gallery, contact info — so attendees can explore the show floor before they even arrive. And with the Expo or Pulse layout pack, you can set up the whole app navigation in minutes instead of building it block by block.

draft.docs_gap: The exhibitor and sponsor guides should add a section explaining how to create and manage Attend app Showrooms and Products, including the photo and product count limits and the permission required.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend app brings your event program, exhibitor directory, and networking tools into a single mobile experience for attendees. Showrooms let each exhibitor tell their story — products, deals, photos, and contact details — directly inside the app, reducing the need for attendees to leave to find information. Layout packs give organizers a starting point that fits the event type, whether that is a trade show floor with badge scanning or a content-forward conference with a personal feed.

entries.title: Mobile App editor gains a draft → publish workflow
entries.summary: The **Publish → Mobile App** editor now uses the same draft-and-publish model as the Site builder. Layout, page templates, home blocks, navigation, theme, and maps changes are saved as a draft (with autosave) and only reach attendees when you click **Publish**. Security and privacy switches — app enabled/disabled, sign-in methods, attendee directory, and push notifications — still take effect immediately on save. A **Discard** action lets you abandon unpublished changes, and a **Preview** shows how the draft will look on the phone canvas before publishing. Org-level app settings (name, tagline, logo, colours, events, media, info pages) follow the same draft model; the org app's **enabled** toggle is now a separate instant control.
entries.use_case: Organizers can now stage layout and branding changes to their attendee mobile app without immediately affecting what attendees see, then publish everything at once when it is ready — useful when preparing a new event's app experience in advance or iterating on design without disrupting a live event.

cs_action.note: This is the API half only; the web-ui-v2 editor PR has not yet merged. The draft/publish UI will not be visible to customers until the companion front-end change ships. Do not proactively announce to customers yet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about staging mobile app changes before an event goes live, or when they report accidentally pushing unfinished app layouts to attendees.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Attend Mobile App (beta) who manages event or org app configuration.
internal.staff_path: Publish → Mobile App (event or org level)
internal.gotchas: The UI half of this feature is in a separate PR (web-ui-v2). Until that ships, the draft endpoints exist in the API but the editor UI does not yet expose them. Existing published settings are unaffected — no data migration. Stale-revision conflicts (409 APP_DRAFT_STALE) can occur if two admins edit simultaneously; the second save will be rejected and the user must reload.
internal.talk_track: You can now build out your entire mobile app layout — home blocks, navigation, theme, maps — save it as a draft, preview it on the phone canvas, and publish only when it is ready. Turning the app on or off, or changing sign-in methods, still happens instantly so you always control access.

draft.docs_gap: The article covering the Site builder's draft/publish model should be extended (or a new Mobile App editor guide created) to document the draft → publish flow for the Attend Mobile App, including which settings are drafted vs. instant, the Preview canvas, Discard, and the org-level enabled toggle.
draft.why_use_it: The Mobile App editor lets you configure the attendee-facing app your participants use during the event — home screen layout, navigation, theme, maps, and org-level branding. A draft model means you can make and preview changes at any time without affecting the live app, and publish only when the experience is complete. Security controls like sign-in methods and the attendee directory remain instant so you always have immediate control over access.

entries.title: Attend app gains sponsor placements, event tracking, and an analytics dashboard
entries.summary: Organizers can now create and manage **Sponsor Placements** in the Attend mobile app — including splash-screen "presented by" banners, home carousels, agenda banners, and promoted partner tiles — each with a schedule window, rotation weight, and creative image. The app tracks **app_open**, **screen_view**, **placement_impression**, **placement_tap**, and other events (batched, offline-safe, anonymous-friendly) and surfaces them in a new **App Analytics** dashboard showing active installs, DAU, push open rates, impression/tap counts, CTR, top screens, and a per-sponsor ROI roll-up.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Attend; then Event → Attend → App → Placements

where.path: Event → Attend → App → Placements (admin CRUD) and Event → Attend → App → Analytics (dashboard)

entries.use_case: Events with sponsors want to deliver measurable in-app exposure and prove ROI. Organizers can assign creative assets to specific placement slots, set live windows, and share a per-sponsor analytics report showing impressions, taps, and CTR — without any third-party ad SDK.

cs_action.note: This is a net-new monetisation surface for Attend. Proactively reach out to customers already using Attend who have sponsor tiers or exhibitor programmes — they are the immediate buyers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how sponsors get visibility inside the Attend app, or when they are building a sponsor prospectus and need measurable digital inventory.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Attend beta who sell sponsorships or have exhibitor programmes and want in-app brand exposure with ROI reporting.
internal.gotchas: Sponsored push notifications are NOT a placement — they go through the existing Attend notification composer. Banner slots require an image_url; text-only placements are not supported on those slots. Impressions require ≥50 % visibility for ≥1 second and dedupe to one per install per placement per 30 minutes, so raw impression counts will be lower than page-view counts. The per-sponsor analytics filter uses accountId query param — share the filtered URL with the sponsor contact, not the full dashboard.
internal.talk_track: You can now sell named slots inside the Attend app — a 'presented by' on the splash screen, a banner on the agenda, a carousel on the home screen — and after the event hand each sponsor a report showing exactly how many attendees saw their creative and tapped through to their profile or website.

draft.docs_gap: The attendee-view guide (and a dedicated Attend app placements guide) should document the available placement slots, creative specs (image dimensions, required vs optional fields), schedule windows, rotation weights, the viewability rules for impressions, and how to read the per-sponsor analytics report.
draft.why_use_it: Sponsor placements let you sell branded inventory inside the Attend mobile app — splash screens, home banners, carousels, agenda banners, and promoted partner tiles — and back every placement with viewability-verified impression and tap data. The analytics dashboard gives you and your sponsors a single source of truth for active installs, daily active users, push performance, and per-placement CTR, so you can price sponsorships with confidence and deliver post-event ROI reports without manual data assembly.

entries.title: Manage sponsor ad placements and view mobile app analytics in Attend
entries.summary: Two new pages are available under the **Attend** nav group for events using the Attend mobile app. **Sponsor Placements** lets organizers create and manage in-app ad slots — choosing the sponsor or exhibitor, placement slot (banner, carousel, etc.), creative image, tap destination, run window, priority, and rotation weight — with a side-sheet editor and live status indicators (**Live / Scheduled / Ended / Off**). **Analytics** shows a configurable date-range dashboard (7 / 14 / 30 / 90 days) with KPIs for installs, sign-ins, daily active users, push opens, saves, and sponsor impressions/taps, a daily chart, top screens/sessions/speakers/sponsors tables, and a per-sponsor breakdown with **CSV export** and a printable per-sponsor report. Two new home-block types — **Sponsor banner** and **Sponsor carousel** — also appear in the App Design block menu when the API supports them.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Attend Mobile App

entries.use_case: Events that sell sponsorships can now give sponsors measurable in-app ad inventory — banners, carousels, and other placements — and share impression, tap, and CTR data directly from the Analytics page, making it easier to demonstrate sponsor ROI and justify renewals.

cs_action.note: The attend_app Early Access gate must be on for the event. Both pages show a 'Couldn't load…' error against an API version that predates the companion API release (PR #4540); confirm the API has been deployed before walking customers through the feature.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to sell or report on in-app sponsor advertising, or when they want engagement metrics for their Attend mobile app.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already using the Attend mobile app beta who have sponsors or exhibitors and want to offer measurable in-app ad placements.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → Sponsor Placements / Attend → Analytics
internal.gotchas: The Sponsor banner and Sponsor carousel home blocks only appear in App Design when the API lists them in layout_options.block_types — an older API version will silently hide them.
