internal.talk_track: You can now sell banner and carousel slots inside your Attend app, set run windows and rotation weights per sponsor, and then share a printable per-sponsor report showing impressions, taps, and CTR — all without leaving Sessionboard.

draft.docs_gap: No existing guide covers Attend Sponsor Placements or the Attend Analytics dashboard; a new guide should document the placement editor fields (slots, creative specs, link types, priority/weight), the Analytics KPI definitions, the CSV export, and the per-sponsor report.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend mobile app puts your event program, networking, and sponsor content in attendees' pockets. Sponsor Placements lets you sell and manage in-app ad slots with full creative control, scheduling, and priority weighting. The Analytics dashboard gives you a real-time view of how attendees engage with the app — from daily active users and push-open rates to per-sponsor impression and tap-through data — so you can make informed decisions about content, communications, and sponsor packages.

entries.title: Attend app: 1:1 messages, meeting requests, People to meet, and networking moderation
entries.summary: The Attend mobile app now includes a full networking suite. Attendees can send **direct messages** to other listed attendees or to sponsor/exhibitor teams, request and manage **meetings** (with slot availability checks, reschedule proposals, and location options including booth and admin-defined meeting places), and browse a personalised **People to meet** list ranked by shared sessions, topics, and saved speakers. Accepted meetings appear in the attendee's **My schedule** calendar feed. Organizers get a new **Attend → Networking** admin page to configure settings, view reports, and moderate content (dismiss, remove a message, or suspend an attendee).

enable.path: Attend → Networking → Settings

where.path: Attend → Networking (admin); Attend mobile app → Messages / Meetings / People to meet (attendee)

entries.use_case: Events that want to drive meaningful connections between attendees, sponsors, and exhibitors can now offer structured networking directly inside the Attend app — no third-party tool required. Organizers can moderate conversations and meetings in real time, and attendees get curated match suggestions based on content they already engaged with.

cs_action.note: Networking is off by default; organizers enable it under Attend → Networking → Settings. CS should walk customers through privacy settings, meeting slot configuration (event days × hours × slot length), and moderation before go-live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the Attend app asks about in-app networking, attendee matchmaking, or wants to reduce reliance on a separate networking tool.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already on the Attend beta who run events where attendee-to-attendee or attendee-to-sponsor networking is a key programme goal.
internal.gotchas: Only attendees listed in the directory can send or receive messages and meeting requests — unlisted, cancelled, or attendees from other events get a 404. A transferred registration starts with an empty inbox. Rate limits apply: 20 messages/min, 30 new conversations/day, 30 meeting requests/day. Meeting slot availability is checked under a per-event lock to prevent double-booking. Push notifications use neutral text (no names or message content).
internal.talk_track: With Attend Networking, your attendees can message each other and request meetings right inside the app they're already using for the schedule. People to meet surfaces the most relevant connections based on sessions and topics they've already engaged with — so the suggestions feel personal, not random. You stay in control with a moderation queue where you can remove messages or suspend bad actors without any back-and-forth with support.

draft.docs_gap: The Attendee view guide should be expanded (or a dedicated Networking guide created) to cover enabling networking, the attendee-facing messages and meetings flows, People to meet opt-in and ranking logic, privacy rules (listed-only reachability, blocks, no-messages/no-meetings preferences), and the admin Attend → Networking moderation page including report resolution and suspensions.
draft.why_use_it: Networking is one of the top reasons people attend events, and the Attend app brings it into the same place attendees already use to browse sessions and manage their schedule. Direct messages let attendees reach out to each other or to sponsor teams without exchanging personal contact details. Meeting requests include availability checks, location options, and calendar integration so confirmed meetings show up automatically in each person's schedule. The People to meet list surfaces relevant connections based on shared sessions, topics, and saved speakers — so attendees spend less time searching and more time having the right conversations.

entries.title: Send push notifications and configure session/exhibitor recommendations in the Attend mobile app
entries.summary: Two new pages are available under the **Attend** navigation group for organizers managing the Attend mobile app. **Attend → Notifications** lets you compose and schedule push notifications with per-language content, targeted **Audience** segments (registrant types, tracks/topics interest, saved items, partner staff, speakers, attended a session, or a list of emails), a live recipient count showing how many have notifications enabled, an **Urgent** flag that bypasses quiet hours, a lock-screen **Preview**, and a **Send a test to me** option before confirming. The notifications list shows delivery reach — recipients, opened %, read %, pushed, capped, waiting, and failed — with options to edit, duplicate, unschedule, or delete. **Attend → Recommendations** lets you toggle AI-powered recommendations on or off, prompt attendees to pick interests after first sign-in, choose which content types (sessions, exhibitors & sponsors) are recommended, set pin/boost/hide rules, and use **Preview as an attendee** to see the ranked list with the same reason lines the app displays.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Attend Mobile App

entries.use_case: Event organizers running the Attend mobile app can now reach attendees directly with targeted push notifications — for example, alerting a specific track's audience about a last-minute room change — and can surface personalised session and exhibitor recommendations so attendees discover content that matches their stated interests without manual curation.

cs_action.note: The Attend Mobile App Early Access gate must be on for the event; the web-api release carrying PR #4543 must also be deployed to prod before these pages load successfully — until then they show a 'couldn't load' error state.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the Attend mobile app asks how to communicate with attendees in-app or wants to surface personalised content recommendations.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who have the Attend Mobile App beta enabled and are actively running the Attend app for their event.
internal.gotchas: Pages show a 'couldn't load' error until the matching web-api release (PR #4543) is in prod. internal.talk_track: With the Notifications page you can target exactly the right slice of your audience — say, everyone who saved a session in Track A — write the message in every event language, preview it on a lock screen, and send a test to yourself before it goes live. Recommendations then do the heavy lifting between sends, automatically ranking sessions and exhibitors for each attendee based on their interests, while your pin and boost rules keep featured content front and centre.

draft.docs_gap: The /communications/notifications article covers internal platform notifications and messaging; it should gain a new section documenting the Attend → Notifications composer (audience segments, live count, urgent flag, scheduling, delivery metrics) and the Attend → Recommendations settings (toggle, onboarding interests prompt, pin/boost/hide rules, and attendee preview).
draft.why_use_it: The Attend mobile app puts your event program in attendees' hands, and the Notifications and Recommendations pages give you the controls to make that experience feel personal and timely. Use Notifications to send targeted messages to specific audience segments — by registrant type, topic interest, saved sessions, or a hand-picked list — and schedule them in advance or send immediately. Use Recommendations to let the app surface the sessions and exhibitors most relevant to each attendee based on their interests, with pin, boost, and hide rules so you stay in control of what rises to the top.

entries.title: Networking settings, activity counts, and moderation queue in Attend

draft.docs_gap: The attendee-view guide does not cover the Networking settings page, activity counts, meeting configuration, or the moderation queue — a dedicated section or new guide is needed for all of these.
draft.why_use_it: The Networking page gives organizers a single place to configure and oversee all attendee-to-attendee interaction in the Attend mobile app. You decide which channels — direct messages, meeting requests, and people-to-meet matching — are available, and you set the rules for how meetings work, including length, hours, and locations tied to your venue map. When attendees flag inappropriate messages, the moderation queue lets you review the content, dismiss false positives, remove harmful messages, or pause a person's networking access entirely.

entries.title: Three new Attend app layout packs: Mosaic, Keynote, and Concierge
entries.summary: The Attend mobile app layout catalog now includes three additional template packs. **Mosaic** uses a photo-grid home screen with configurable tile rows and optional colour wash. **Keynote** features hero cards on the home screen, curated agenda groups, a cinematic session view, a photo carousel for people, and optional **Presented by** sponsor attribution under key art. **Concierge** adds a **meetings-first** agenda view, a **minimal** session view, a **home-only** nav bar (Home · Agenda · Meetings · Me), and two new content blocks — **band** (a title with up to 6 sub-link tiles and an optional destination) and **sponsor-line** (a title and tier label).

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the Mosaic, Keynote, or Concierge layout pack; then configure it under the Attend app builder for your event.

entries.use_case: Events that want a visually distinct mobile app experience can now choose from three purpose-built layout packs — a photo-grid style for community-driven conferences (Mosaic), a cinematic hero-card style for flagship keynote events (Keynote), or a concierge-style layout that surfaces networking meetings alongside the agenda (Concierge).

cs_action.note: These packs are registered server-side; the matching mobile and admin PRs are still pending on the same branch. Confirm all three PRs are merged before positioning to a customer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer on the Attend beta asks for a more visually differentiated app or needs networking meetings surfaced prominently in the mobile experience.
internal.who_should_get_it: Attend beta customers — particularly those running flagship keynote events, photo-forward community conferences, or events with a strong networking/meetings programme.
internal.gotchas: Mobile and admin PRs are described as follow-on work on the same branch; the layout catalog changes are server-side only in this PR. Do not promise the full UI to customers until all three PRs are confirmed merged. The Concierge meetings-first agenda and minimal session views are net-new layout values — verify the mobile client supports them before enabling.
internal.talk_track: We now have three new app layout packs you can choose from. Mosaic gives you a photo-grid home screen great for community events; Keynote puts a cinematic hero front and centre with optional sponsor attribution; and Concierge is built for events where networking meetings are as important as the agenda — it surfaces meetings right in the nav alongside sessions.

draft.docs_gap: No guide currently documents the Attend app layout catalog or its template packs; a new article should cover how to select a pack, what each pack's home/agenda/session/nav templates look like, and how to configure pack-specific options such as Mosaic row sizes and wash, Keynote hero presented-by and home tabs, and Concierge band and sponsor-line blocks.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend app layout catalog lets organizers match the look and feel of their mobile app to the character of their event without custom development. Each pack ships with a coordinated set of home, agenda, session, and navigation templates so the app feels intentional from the first screen. Packs are validated at draft and publish time, so configuration errors surface before attendees see them.

entries.title: Attend app Overview page and QR share poster PDF
entries.summary: The **Attend** app admin now has an **Overview** page that shows app status (on/off, Early Access, sign-in methods, publish state), a setup checklist (**Sign In**, **Design**, **Maps**, **People**, **Notifications**, **Test Sign In**, plus optional **Sponsors**, **Showrooms**, **Posters**), live stats (signed-in attendees, active installs, networking activity, notifications, showrooms), and a recent-activity feed of sign-ins, moderation reports, and sent campaigns. From the same page, organizers can download a one-page **Share Poster** PDF containing the event name and a QR code that links directly to the Attend app sign-in URL.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Attend Mobile App

entries.use_case: Organizers launching the Attend mobile app can check at a glance whether the app is fully configured and ready for attendees, monitor live engagement during the event, and hand printed QR-code posters to venue staff so attendees can scan and sign in instantly.

cs_action.note: This is the API layer only; the matching web-ui-v2 PR is required before the page is visible to customers. Confirm both are deployed before promoting.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer is setting up or actively running the Attend mobile app and wants a health-check dashboard or a quick way to get attendees into the app on-site.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Attend Mobile App beta.
internal.gotchas: The web-UI PR (web-ui-v2) had not merged at the time of this API PR — the endpoint exists but the page may not yet be visible in the product. CJK characters in the event name are silently dropped from the share poster PDF rather than causing an error.
internal.talk_track: The Overview page tells you in seconds whether your Attend app is ready to go — green checklist, live attendee count, and a PDF poster with a QR code you can print and stick on every door.

draft.docs_gap: The /marketing/attendee-view guide should be updated (or a new Attend app admin guide created) to document the Overview page, its checklist items, live stats, activity feed, and the Share Poster PDF download.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend app Overview gives you a single place to confirm your mobile app is set up correctly before doors open and to watch real-time engagement — installs, sign-ins, networking activity, and notifications — while the event is live. The setup checklist flags every required step (sign-in method, design, maps, directory, notifications) and optional extras (sponsors, showrooms, posters) so nothing is missed. The downloadable QR share poster lets you put a scannable link anywhere in the venue without needing a separate design tool.

entries.title: Exhibitor staff can scan attendee badges and capture leads in the Attend app
entries.summary: Sponsor and exhibitor team members open the Attend mobile app, scan an attendee's badge QR code, and instantly capture a lead shared across their whole team. Each lead can include a **Hot / Warm / Cold** rating, notes, tags, and answers to the team's own qualifying questions. Attendees control whether their email is shared via a **Share my email with exhibitors** consent toggle. Organizers manage every team's licence, seat holders, and settings under **Attend → Partners → Lead retrieval**, and can export all leads to CSV.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable lead retrieval and assign seats; then Attend → Partners → Lead retrieval

entries.use_case: Events with exhibitors and sponsors need a way for booth staff to capture and qualify attendee interest on the show floor without paper forms or third-party scanners. With lead retrieval in the Attend app, exhibitor teams scan badges, rate leads, and share the full list in real time — and organizers can prove ROI to sponsors with per-team counts and a consent-safe CSV export.

cs_action.note: Seats are 0 by default — no exhibitor can scan until the organizer's team is licensed and seats are assigned. CS must provision Attend_Lead_Licenses per team before go-live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how sponsors or exhibitors can capture leads at their event, or when they are evaluating third-party badge-scanning vendors.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running trade shows, expos, or conferences with paying sponsors or exhibitors who expect lead retrieval as part of their package.
internal.gotchas: Email is never stored on the lead record — it is read live from the attendee's profile, so if an attendee withdraws consent after a scan the email disappears from that lead immediately. Printed-badge QR codes (vendor badge_id / source_attendee_id) are only resolved when the organizer explicitly enables that option. Cross-event badge codes return badge_unknown. The mobile and admin UI PRs (sessionboard-mobile, sessionboard-web-ui-v2) are follow-ons — this PR is API only.
internal.talk_track: Your exhibitors get a shared lead list the moment they scan a badge — no separate scanner hardware, no post-event data reconciliation. You control which fields they see, attendees control whether their email is shared, and you can pull a consent-safe CSV for every team at the end of the event.

draft.docs_gap: No existing guide covers the Attend app lead retrieval feature. A new article should document: enabling lead retrieval, assigning seats to exhibitor teams, the attendee badge QR and email-consent toggle, how exhibitor staff scan and qualify leads in the Attend app, and how organizers export leads via the Lead retrieval admin page.
draft.why_use_it: Lead retrieval lets exhibitor and sponsor staff capture attendee contact details by scanning badge QR codes directly in the Attend mobile app. Leads are shared instantly across the whole booth team, can be rated Hot / Warm / Cold, enriched with notes and qualifying-question answers, and exported by the organizer. Attendee email consent is respected live — opting out removes the address from every lead already taken — so exhibitors always work with permission-safe data.

entries.title: Attend app gets an AI assistant that answers questions about the event
entries.summary: A new **Ask** tab in the Attend mobile app lets attendees ask natural-language questions about the event — sessions, speakers, maps, exhibitors — and receive streamed, cited answers grounded exclusively in that event's published data. Organizers can configure **Ask** from the admin panel, including enabling or disabling it, setting a daily question allowance per attendee, a daily AI budget, and suggested starter questions; a 7-day usage dashboard shows questions asked, attendees reached, AI spend, and top cited items.

enable.path: Attend → Engage → Ask → Settings (admin panel)

entries.use_case: Attendees at large conferences often struggle to find the right session, locate a booth, or remember a speaker's name mid-event. Ask lets them type a question in plain language and get an instant, cited answer drawn from the live program — without leaving the app or hunting through the schedule.

cs_action.note: Ask is off by default. The organizer must enable it in the Attend admin panel (Attend → Engage → Ask → Settings) and the org must have AI features enabled (flag_enable_ai_features). Confirm the org has the Attend app feature before raising it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running a large event asks how attendees can self-serve schedule or speaker information without overwhelming the help desk.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with the Attend mobile app (beta) who have AI features enabled at the org level and want to reduce attendee support load during the event.
internal.staff_path: Attend admin panel → Engage → Ask → Settings; usage dashboard shows 7-day metrics
internal.gotchas: Ask is grounded only in public event data — no attendee PII, no embargoed abstracts, no draft sessions. Daily per-attendee question caps and a rolling 24-hour event budget apply; if the budget is exhausted, Ask refuses new questions gracefully. The add_to_schedule action is queued through the app's saves queue, not written directly. History is stored per attendee and re-rendered against the current program on each load.
internal.talk_track: Attendees can open the Ask tab, type 'What sessions on AI are happening after lunch?' or 'Where is booth 1044?' and get a cited answer in seconds — no scrolling through the full schedule. You set the daily question limit and a spend cap so costs stay predictable.

draft.docs_gap: The attendee-view guide should add a section documenting the Ask tab: how attendees access it, what kinds of questions it can answer, how citations work, and how organizers configure and monitor it from the admin panel.
draft.why_use_it: Ask is an AI assistant built into the Attend app that answers attendee questions about the event — sessions, speakers, exhibitors, maps, and more — using only that event's published data. Answers stream in real time with numbered citations so attendees can tap through to the source. Organizers control daily question limits, AI spend caps, and the starter questions shown on the home screen, and can review a 7-day usage dashboard to understand how attendees are engaging with the feature.

entries.title: Three new mobile app layout packs: Mosaic, Keynote and Concierge
entries.summary: **Publish → Mobile App** now offers three additional layout packs alongside the existing Atlas, Scholar, Expo and Pulse options. **Mosaic** displays edge-to-edge photo grids with configurable **Photos per row** and a **Colour wash over photos** option. **Keynote** adds a full-bleed hero with a **Show Presented by** sponsor line, glass-card navigation tiles, home tabs (**Discover · For you · Streaming**), a cinematic session header with a play button, and a featured speakers rail. **Concierge** introduces text **band** blocks (each with up to 6 sub-links), a **sponsor-line** block, a "My meetings" section before the agenda, and a minimal session view with no image or tabs — all with a Back button instead of a tab bar on inner pages.
entries.use_case: Events with strong visual branding (Mosaic), keynote-driven programming (Keynote), or concierge-style networking and supplier experiences (Concierge) can now pick a layout that matches their event's personality without custom development. Each pack ships with its own inspector controls so organizers can tune the look directly in the app editor.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks for a more visually distinctive or content-structured mobile app experience beyond the existing Atlas/Scholar/Expo/Pulse options.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already using the Attend Mobile App (beta) who want a layout tailored to photo-heavy, keynote-driven, or concierge/networking-focused events.

internal.talk_track: You can now pick Mosaic for a photo-grid home screen, Keynote for a cinematic hero with sponsor branding and streaming tabs, or Concierge for a text-band navigation style with suite sponsors and a meetings-first agenda — all configured right in the app editor with a live phone preview.

draft.docs_gap: No guide currently documents the Attend Mobile App layout picker or any of its packs; a new article should cover how to open the layout picker, what each pack offers, and how to use the per-pack inspector controls (Photos per row, Colour wash, Show Presented by, home tabs, band blocks, sponsor-line blocks).
draft.why_use_it: The Attend Mobile App layout picker lets organizers choose a visual structure that fits their event's brand and attendee journey — from photo-forward grids to cinematic hero art to text-band navigation. Each pack controls the home screen, session detail, and inner-page chrome, so the app feels purpose-built for the event rather than generic. Inspector controls for each pack let organizers adjust key design options — sponsor placement, row sizes, colour washes, home tabs — without touching code. Packs are available immediately in the app editor and render live in the WYSIWYG phone canvas.

entries.title: Manage lead retrieval licences, seats, settings and exports for exhibitors and sponsors
entries.summary: A new **Lead Retrieval** page under **Attend → Partners** lets organizers control every aspect of badge-scanning lead capture. The **Exhibitors and Sponsors** table shows each team's access level (**Event default / Licensed / Off**), editable seat counts (0–1000, saved on blur or Enter), a seat-holder popover with a **Release** action, per-rating lead counts, last-scan time, and a per-team **CSV export**; the header action exports all leads for the event. **Settings** covers lead retrieval on/off, default seats per team, which contact fields a scan shares (name always; job title, company, email — email only for attendees who opt in on **My badge**), printed badge scan types (Sessionboard check-in QR, badge number, provider attendee ID), and per-language consent text (en/de/es/fr). Summary totals at the top show total leads, hot leads, teams scanning, and seats in use vs. licensed.
entries.use_case: Events that offer badge-scanning as an exhibitor or sponsor benefit can now manage every team's access level, seat count, and data-sharing rules from one page — and pull a full CSV of leads per team or for the whole event without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: The page is gated behind the Attend beta. The API (web-api PR #4550) must be deployed before the page is functional; until then it shows a 'not on this server yet' notice rather than an error. CRM push from team lead retrieval into each team's CRM is a planned follow-up, not yet available.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how exhibitors or sponsors will capture leads at their event, or when they are evaluating the Attend mobile app for on-site badge scanning.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running trade shows, expos, or conferences where exhibitors and sponsors expect lead retrieval as part of their package.
internal.gotchas: Email is only shared for attendees who opt in via My badge — warn customers not to promise exhibitors full email capture without confirming attendee opt-in rates. Badge-number and provider-attendee-ID scan types carry a warning in the UI that numbers can be guessable. CRM push per team is not yet available (Apps follow-up).
internal.talk_track: With Lead Retrieval in Attend, you can give each exhibitor or sponsor exactly the number of scanning seats they paid for, see in real time how many leads each team has captured and at what rating, and export the full list to CSV — all without leaving Sessionboard.

draft.docs_gap: No existing guide covers the Lead Retrieval page in Attend. A new article should document the Exhibitors and Sponsors table (access levels, seat management, seat-holder popover, Release action, CSV export), the Settings card (on/off toggle, default seats, scan-shared fields, badge scan types, consent text per language), and the summary totals at the top of the page.
draft.why_use_it: Lead retrieval lets exhibitors and sponsors scan attendee badges at your event to capture contact details instantly. Organizers control which teams have access, how many seats each team holds, what attendee data a scan shares, and how consent is presented — all from a single page. Per-team and event-wide CSV exports make it straightforward to reconcile scanning activity and hand off lead data after the event.

entries.title: Configure and monitor the Attend app's Ask AI assistant
entries.summary: A new **Ask** settings page is available under the Attend app admin (Engage → **Ask**). Organizers can enable the assistant, set a per-attendee daily question limit, cap the daily AI spend (USD), and define up to six starter questions. A **Usage (last 7 days)** panel shows questions asked today and over the week, unique attendees, AI cost vs. budget, the share of questions answered without a source (a content-gap signal), schedule adds, limited responses, declined/failed responses, and the most-cited content items. Question text is never displayed in the usage panel.

enable.path: Attend App → Engage → Ask → Assistant → enable toggle

entries.use_case: Events that want to give attendees an in-app AI concierge can now turn on Ask, guard against runaway AI costs with a daily budget cap, and use the usage panel to spot content gaps — sessions or topics that the assistant cannot answer from published content — so organizers know what to fill in before the event.

cs_action.note: The page depends on a matching web-api release (PR #4551). Confirm that release is live in prod before pointing customers to this page — an older API returns a 404.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about attendee self-service, wayfinding, or reducing help-desk load during the event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already using the Attend mobile app (beta) who want to add an AI Q&A layer for attendees.

internal.talk_track: You can give every attendee an always-on AI assistant that answers questions from your published agenda and speaker content. Set a daily budget so costs stay predictable, and check the usage panel after day one to see which topics the assistant couldn't answer — that's your content gap list.

draft.docs_gap: No existing guide covers the Attend app's Ask feature; a new article should document how to enable Ask, configure limits and starter questions, read the usage panel, and interpret the content-gap signal.

You control how many questions each attendee can ask per day and how much the AI can spend in 24 hours, so the feature scales to any event size without surprise costs. The usage dashboard shows which content is cited most often and flags questions the assistant could not answer from a source, giving you a clear signal of where to add or improve session descriptions, speaker bios, or schedule details.

entries.title: Live Q&A, polls, and session evaluations in the Attend app
entries.summary: Attendees can now ask questions, upvote others' questions, vote in polls, and complete session and speaker evaluations directly inside the Attend mobile app. Organizers manage everything from the new **Attend → Live engagement** admin section, which includes settings, a per-session moderation queue, and a polls manager. Speakers can open and close polls from the stage. When a session's credit designation requires an evaluation for CE/CME claiming, the app evaluation doubles as the claim evidence so attendees are never asked to evaluate twice.

enable.path: Attend → Live engagement → Settings

entries.use_case: Medical and scientific societies running accredited sessions need in-room Q&A, live polling, and post-session evaluations — the same capabilities offered by Cadmium, Sherpa, and Amego. Organizers can now deliver all three natively in the Attend app without a third-party tool, and tie the evaluation directly to CE/CME credit claiming so attendees complete it only once.

cs_action.note: This is a major new capability for medical/scientific society customers. Proactively reach out to accounts currently using Cadmium, Sherpa, or Amego for in-room engagement — they are the primary target.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about in-room audience engagement, live polling, session Q&A, or post-session evaluations for accredited events.
internal.who_should_get_it: Medical and scientific society customers, or any customer using the Attend app who runs accredited sessions or wants structured audience interaction.
internal.gotchas: The companion mobile app (sessionboard-mobile) and the admin UI (web-ui-v2) PRs must merge after this API PR — the feature is not fully usable until all three ship. Evaluation results are aggregate-only for speakers until at least 3 responses are collected. CE/CME gating requires the session's credit designation to have claim_gates.eval set and the claim site to have an eval survey configured.
internal.talk_track: The Attend app now has built-in Q&A with moderation, single/multiple-choice and word-cloud polls that speakers can open from the stage, and session evaluations that feed directly into CE/CME credit claiming — so your attendees evaluate once and get credit automatically.

entries.title: Moderate Q&A, run polls, and track evaluations from a new Live Engagement page
entries.summary: A new **Attend › Live Engagement** page gives event staff a real-time control centre for in-session audience interaction. From the session list, organizers can open any session and switch between three tabs: **Q&A** (approve, hide, mark answered, or move questions between queues; toggle Q&A open/closed), **Polls** (create single-choice, multiple-choice, or word-cloud polls; open, close, or reopen them; view live result bars and word counts), and **Evaluation** (see which survey applies, the response count, and a direct link to survey results). Use it to track real-time attendance numbers, moderate networking reports, manage lead retrieval teams, and tune session engagement features like polls and Q&A, all without leaving Sessionboard.

entries.title: Check in to sessions, reserve seats and take CE quizzes in the Attend app
entries.summary: Attendees can check in to sessions in the Attend app — with a **Check in** button, by scanning the room's QR poster, or by a room monitor scanning their badge — and check out again when the event counts time in the room. Sessions can require a reserved seat with a waitlist, and a session's CE quiz can be taken in the app's **Credits** tab; a pass unlocks the credit claim.

enable.path: Attend → Engagement → Check-in & seats → Ways to check in

where.path: Attend app → session → check-in card; Credits tab → Take the quiz

entries.use_case: Accredited meetings have to show who was in the room and for how long. Check-in in the app records that per session, straight into the attendance the credit claim reads, without paper sign-in sheets or a separate scanning vendor — and attendees finish the session quiz before they leave the room.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a medical, scientific or professional society that awards CE/CME credit asks how they prove who was in the room, for how long, or wants seat caps and waitlists for popular sessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events on the Attend Mobile App beta that award continuing-education credit through Lessons & Credits, or run sessions with limited seats.

cs_action.note: Off until the organizer picks a check-in method. Needs the web-api release that carries lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4575 and the Attend app build from lennd/sessionboard-mobile#72; older app builds hide the check-in card and keep quiz-gated credit as staff-only.

internal.gotchas: A Check in button tap is recorded as self-reported attendance; room QR and monitor scans are recorded as check-ins, so the claims audit tells them apart. The app only asks for a quiz on credit that requires a quiz pass, and the session Credits panel cannot set that requirement yet (only Evaluation required) — staff set it until lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4577 adds it. The quiz is written on the lesson made from the session (Create on-demand lesson → Knowledge check), which needs the org's lesson Paths.
internal.talk_track: Pick how people check in — a button, a QR poster on each door, or your staff scanning badges — and turn on check-out if credit depends on time in the room. Whatever they use, attendance lands where the credit claim looks for it, and a quiz passed in the app unlocks the claim.

entries.title: Check-in & seats: session check-in rules, seat limits, waitlists and attendance exports
entries.summary: A **Check-in & seats** tab under **Attend → Engagement** sets how attendees check in, a minimum time in the room for duration-based credit, capacity enforcement and the release of no-shows' reservations. Each session gets **Seats**, **Require a reservation** and **Waitlist when full**, a page listing who checked in and who reserved, and a quiz pass mark and attempts limit. **Room QR posters**, **Export check-ins** and **Export reservations** download posters and CSVs.

enable.path: Attend → Engagement → Check-in & seats

entries.use_case: Organizers see live who is in each room against its capacity, cap popular sessions with reservations and a waitlist that fills itself when no-shows are released, and hand their accreditor a per-session check-in export instead of reconciling sign-in sheets.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a medical, scientific or professional society that awards CE/CME credit asks how they prove who was in the room, for how long, or wants seat caps and waitlists for popular sessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events on the Attend Mobile App beta that award continuing-education credit through Lessons & Credits, or run sessions with limited seats.

cs_action.note: The tab shows “Room check-in is coming” until the region runs the web-api release with lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4575.

internal.gotchas: Seat limits fall back to the room's capacity when a session has none. Room monitors are registrations, not team members, and need “Room monitors scan badges” ticked. The Quiz column and quiz card only appear once the lesson made from the session has a quiz.
internal.talk_track: Open Check-in & seats during the event and you see every room filling up; click a session for who is in, for how long, and whether their attendance counts yet, then export it for your accreditor.

entries.title: Annotate session slides and export notes as a PDF in the Attend app
entries.summary: Attendees can now page through a session's released slide decks in the Attend mobile app, draw on each slide with a **Pen**, **Highlighter**, or **Eraser**, type a typed note per slide, and tap **Export My Notes** to download a PDF that combines their drawings, slides, typed notes, and saved session moments. Annotations sync automatically across devices and are restored after a reinstall. Organizers can toggle the feature under **Attend App Settings → Slide Notes**.
entries.use_case: Conference attendees who want to capture ideas during a presentation can draw directly on slides and type notes per page, then walk away with a single PDF that includes every annotated slide alongside their session notes — no separate note-taking app needed.

cs_action.note: Slide Notes is on by default for events using the Attend app. Organizers can turn it off under Attend App Settings → Slide Notes if they do not want attendees annotating slides.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how attendees can take notes during sessions, or when they are looking for ways to increase engagement with uploaded session content.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Attend mobile app (beta) who uploads PDF or PowerPoint slide decks to sessions.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → App Settings → Slide Notes
internal.gotchas: Only PDF and Filestack-hosted PPTX files render as annotatable slides; PPTX files stored only in the Sessionboard bucket show as 'unsupported' for drawing (typed notes still work). Up to 200 pages per deck and 5,000 annotated pages per attendee per event. The organizer-side toggle and the mobile app UI ship in separate follow-up PRs — this PR is the API layer only.
internal.talk_track: Attendees can now open any released slide deck right in the app, draw on slides, type notes per page, and export a polished PDF of everything they annotated — it's a built-in note-taking experience that keeps all their conference insights in one place.

entries.title: Control whether attendees can annotate and export session slides in the mobile app
entries.summary: A **Slide notes** switch in **Attend → Mobile App → Event app settings** lets organizers enable or disable the slide-annotation feature for attendees. When on (the default), attendees can page through released session slides, draw on them, type a note per slide, and export their notes as a PDF from the mobile app.

where.path: Attend → Mobile App → Event app settings → Slide notes

entries.use_case: Events that release session slides to attendees can let participants annotate each slide and export a personal PDF of their notes — useful for educational or training conferences where attendees want to keep a record. Organizers who prefer a cleaner app experience or have not released slides can turn the feature off entirely.

cs_action.note: The switch is hidden until the companion web-api release (sessionboard-web-api#4574) is live. Confirm that release is deployed before telling customers the feature is available.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how attendees can engage with session slides in the app, or when they want to offer note-taking or study-aid features at an educational or training event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Attend mobile app (beta) who release session slides to attendees and want to give participants a way to annotate and export them.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → Mobile App → Event app settings → Slide notes
internal.gotchas: The switch is hidden and never sent to the API until the web-api counterpart (sessionboard-web-api#4574) is deployed. Do not promise the feature to customers until both releases are confirmed live.
internal.talk_track: With Slide notes on, your attendees can flip through the slides you release, draw on them, add a typed note to each one, and export the whole thing as a PDF — great for workshops or CME sessions where people want to keep their notes.

entries.title: Attend app: read live captions in your own language, and limit which app languages an event offers
entries.summary: Attendees in the Attend mobile app can now switch live captions to their preferred language mid-session using **Caption Language**; captions are translated in real time (powered by DeepL) while the original captions continue for everyone else. Organizers can also set an ordered list of allowed app languages per event via **App Settings → Languages**, restricting which of the 33 supported languages attendees can choose from (leaving the list empty restores all languages).

where.path: Attend → App Settings → Languages (organizer limit); Attend app → session → Caption Language (attendee)

entries.use_case: Events with multilingual audiences can let each attendee read live captions in their own language without disrupting the original caption feed for others. Organizers running focused regional events can restrict the language menu to only the languages relevant to their audience.

cs_action.note: Translation is powered by DeepL. A per-event rolling 24-hour spend ceiling (default $25 USD, configurable via ATTEND_LIVE_TRANSLATION_DAILY_COST_CEILING_USD) pauses translation and notifies attendees with a 'paused' status when hit. The DeepL API key is shared across environments; if quota is exhausted, the feature degrades gracefully to original-only captions without errors. The organizer-side language-limit UI is not yet built (follow-up in web-ui-v2), so the languages list can only be set via API for now.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about multilingual event support or says they cannot find an event app that works in multiple languages.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running international or multilingual conferences who use live transcription/captions in the Attend app.
internal.staff_path: Attend → App Settings (API only for language list until admin UI ships)
internal.gotchas: 1) The organizer UI for restricting app languages is not yet available — it must be set via API (PUT …/app/settings { languages }). 2) The DeepL spend ceiling defaults to $25/event/day; if hit, captions revert to original-only and attendees see a 'paused' indicator. 3) Interim (partial) caption lines are never translated — only final captions. 4) Every event's app bundle digest changes once on deploy, causing a one-time refetch for all attendees.
internal.talk_track: Attendees can now tap Caption Language in the session view and read live captions in their own language — up to 33 languages — while the original captions keep flowing for everyone else. You can also lock down which languages appear in the picker so the app feels tailored to your audience.

entries.title: Set a LinkedIn company page ID so the app's "Add to LinkedIn profile" feature shows your organization's logo
entries.summary: A new **Add to LinkedIn profile** card appears in **Attend → Networking**. It explains what speakers and attendees can add to their LinkedIn profiles from the app, and lets admins enter an optional **LinkedIn company page ID** (the number in `linkedin.com/company/<id>/admin`). When set, LinkedIn displays the organization's page and logo as the issuer; without it, only the organization's name is used. The ID is set once per organization and applies to all its events.

where.path: Attend → Networking → Add to LinkedIn profile

entries.use_case: Organizations that want attendees and speakers to share their participation on LinkedIn can enter their LinkedIn company page ID so the credential or badge shows the organization's verified logo and page — not just a plain text name — giving the listing more credibility and visibility.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to make LinkedIn profile additions from the app show their organization's logo or branded page instead of just a name.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Attend app (beta) who actively promote LinkedIn sharing as part of their event networking or speaker engagement strategy.
internal.staff_path: Attend → Networking → Add to LinkedIn profile card
internal.gotchas: The card is hidden (returns 404) until web-api PR #4572 is deployed — do not surface this to customers until both PRs are live. The LinkedIn company page ID is the numeric ID from the /admin URL of the company page, not the vanity name. The setting is org-level and applies to all events under that organization.
internal.talk_track: Once you enter your LinkedIn company page ID in the Attend Networking settings, any profile additions your speakers or attendees make through the app will show your organization's logo and link directly to your LinkedIn company page — a much stronger brand impression than a plain text name.

entries.title: Attendees can add speaker, CE credit, or attendance credentials to their LinkedIn profile from the app
entries.summary: A new **Add to LinkedIn Profile** action in the Attend mobile app lets attendees add a **Licenses & certifications** entry to their LinkedIn profile in one tap — no LinkedIn login required on Sessionboard's side. Three credential types are available based on the event's configuration: **Speaker** (for confirmed speakers with a public session), **CE Credit** (for events using credits), and **Attendee** (once the event has started). Organizers can set their LinkedIn company page ID under event LinkedIn settings so the org's logo appears on the credential.

where.path: Attend → App → (attendee-facing) Profile or session detail → Add to LinkedIn Profile

entries.use_case: Events that award CE credits or feature prominent speakers can let attendees instantly document their participation on LinkedIn, increasing the perceived value of attending and giving speakers a frictionless way to showcase their contribution. Organizers with a LinkedIn company page ID configured get their logo displayed on every credential issued.

cs_action.note: Organizers who want their LinkedIn company logo to appear on credentials must set their LinkedIn company page ID. Prompt them to find this in their LinkedIn Company Page URL and enter it in the event's LinkedIn settings.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to increase attendee engagement or post-event value, or when they run a CE-credit event or have prominent speakers who would benefit from showcasing participation.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Attend mobile app (beta), especially those running CE-credit events or events with keynote/featured speakers.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → (admin) LinkedIn Profile Settings → organizationId field
internal.gotchas: The LinkedIn company page ID must be numeric only; non-numeric values are rejected. The org's LinkedIn ID is stored at the organization level (one per org), not per event — updating it affects all events under that org. The Publish action on Mobile App settings replaces the org metadata JSON wholesale, so the LinkedIn org ID must not be overwritten by an unrelated Mobile App publish.
internal.talk_track: Attendees can now tap one button in the app to add a Speaker, CE Credit, or Attendee credential straight to their LinkedIn profile — no extra login, no copy-pasting. If you add your LinkedIn company page ID in the event settings, your org's logo shows up on every credential your attendees publish.

entries.title: Attendees can display a Verified on LinkedIn badge in the app
entries.summary: Attendees who connect their LinkedIn account can opt in to show a **Verified on LinkedIn** badge on their profile, in the **People** directory, **People I Met**, and message threads. The badge is shown only while LinkedIn has confirmed verification within the last 7 days and the attendee has opted in; disconnecting LinkedIn removes it immediately.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Verified on LinkedIn; then Attend → Networking → People directory

where.path: Attend app → People / People I Met / Messages / Profile

entries.use_case: Events focused on professional networking can give attendees a way to signal verified identity, increasing trust when connecting with new people. Attendees who have completed LinkedIn's identity verification can surface that credential directly in the app without any extra steps.

cs_action.note: Requires the LinkedIn app in the developer portal to have the 'Verified on LinkedIn' product added (Development tier first, then Lite for production) and the environment flag ATTEND_LINKEDIN_VERIFIED_ENABLED=true set in Doppler. This is a multi-step LinkedIn developer portal request — coordinate with engineering before promising to a customer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running a professional or executive-audience event asks how to increase trust and quality of attendee networking connections.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with the Attend mobile app enabled who run events where professional credibility matters — executive summits, financial services, healthcare, or any event where attendees want to vet who they are meeting.
internal.staff_path: Attend → Networking → People directory (badge appears inline on attendee cards)
internal.gotchas: The feature is flagged off by default (ATTEND_LINKEDIN_VERIFIED_ENABLED). Enabling the LinkedIn scope without the LinkedIn developer portal product approved will break all LinkedIn connects for that app — do not enable the flag until LinkedIn has confirmed r_verify_details is active. Badge is hidden if LinkedIn data is older than 7 days; the app re-checks once per day while the badge is showing.
internal.talk_track: Attendees who have verified their identity on LinkedIn can now show that badge right on their profile and in the People directory, so everyone they meet knows they are who they say they are — no extra steps required.

entries.title: Configure Apple Wallet and Google Wallet passes for attendee badges
entries.summary: A new **Wallet pass** card on the Attend → Networking admin page lets organizers enable digital badge passes for attendees. Toggle **Offer Add to Wallet** to let attendees save their badge to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet, and optionally enter a **venue latitude** and **longitude** so the pass surfaces automatically on the attendee's lock screen when they arrive at the venue.
entries.use_case: Organizers running in-person events can let attendees save their badge directly to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet. Adding venue coordinates means the pass appears on the attendee's lock screen when they are near the venue, reducing check-in friction.

cs_action.note: The card is visible in the UI only after the companion API (web-api #4567) is deployed. Until then the card renders nothing on a 404. Confirm API is live before pointing customers to this setting.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about digital badges, contactless check-in, or reducing badge printing costs for in-person events.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Attend beta who run in-person events and want to offer Apple Wallet or Google Wallet badge passes to attendees.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → Networking → Wallet pass card
internal.gotchas: The card is hidden (renders nothing) until the API release (web-api #4567) is live. Apple and Google Wallet must be configured server-side first — the card shows status badges indicating whether each provider is set up. Venue latitude and longitude must both be provided or both left blank; partial entry is blocked inline.
internal.talk_track: Once Wallet passes are configured on the server, you can flip the Offer Add to Wallet switch and optionally drop in your venue coordinates — attendees will then see an Add to Wallet button and their pass will pop up on their lock screen when they walk in the door.

entries.title: Add your event badge to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet from the Attend app
entries.summary: Attendees can now save their event badge directly to their mobile wallet. In the Attend app, the **My Badge** screen gains an **Add to Apple Wallet** button (iOS) and an **Add to Google Wallet** button (Android). The pass shows the attendee's name, event name, localized dates, venue location, and the same scannable **SBB1:** code as the on-screen badge. Organizers enable the feature per event and can supply venue coordinates so the pass surfaces automatically when the attendee arrives.

enable.path: Event → Attend App Settings → Wallet → Enable wallet passes; then supply venue latitude and longitude

where.path: Attend mobile app → My Badge → Add to Apple Wallet / Add to Google Wallet

entries.use_case: Attendees at large conferences can save their badge to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet before arriving, so they can be scanned at the door without opening the app or finding a confirmation email. Organizers with venue coordinates set get the added benefit of the pass surfacing automatically on the attendee's lock screen when they reach the venue.

cs_action.note: Apple and Google wallet credentials must be provisioned in Doppler by the engineering team before the organizer-facing toggle has any effect. The toggle and venue fields are visible in event settings only when both credential sets are present in the environment.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about contactless or offline badge access, or when they are running a high-volume check-in event and want to reduce app-open friction at the door.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already using the Attend mobile app for badge scanning who want a smoother attendee check-in experience.
internal.gotchas: Both Apple and Google credentials must be configured in the server environment (Doppler) before the feature is available to any organizer. If only one wallet's credentials are present, only that wallet's button appears. Pass updates after a name or branding change are not yet supported — attendees must re-add the pass to get updated information.
internal.talk_track: With wallet passes enabled, your attendees save their badge once and it lives in Apple Wallet or Google Wallet alongside their boarding pass. No app open needed at the door — just tap or scan. If you give us your venue coordinates, the pass even pops up on their lock screen when they walk in.

entries.title: Attendees can exchange contacts by scanning each other's badge QR code in the Attend app
entries.summary: A new **People I met** feature lets any signed-in attendee scan another attendee's **My badge** QR code to save each other's contact details instantly — name, photo, job title, and company always transfer; email and LinkedIn sharing are controlled by each attendee's own privacy switches. Organizers enable the feature from the admin **Networking** page; attendees manage their sharing preferences in their own networking profile settings.

enable.path: Event → Attend → Networking → Contact Exchange (toggle on)

where.path: Attend app → My badge / People I met

entries.use_case: Events focused on networking can let attendees build a digital contact list on the spot — just scan a badge and both people have each other saved. Attendees control whether their email or LinkedIn travels with the exchange, so consent is built in without requiring a separate directory opt-in.

cs_action.note: Organizer must turn on the Contact Exchange toggle on the admin Networking page; it is off by default. No attendee directory opt-in is required — showing the QR code in person serves as consent.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how attendees can network or exchange contact info at their event using the Attend app.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already using the Attend app (beta) who want structured attendee-to-attendee networking without a separate lead-retrieval or directory product.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → Networking → Contact Exchange toggle
internal.gotchas: Exchange is off by default per event. Email sharing is off by default per attendee; LinkedIn sharing is on by default. Live share switches mean turning off email or LinkedIn hides it retroactively from everyone who already saved that person's contact. Blocks, suspensions, and cancelled/transferred registrations silently decline exchanges without revealing the reason to the scanner. Rate limit is 30 exchanges per minute per registration. This PR is the API layer only — mobile and web-ui-v2 PRs ship separately.
internal.talk_track: Attendees open the app, tap My badge, and let someone scan their QR code — both people instantly have each other saved under People I met, with full control over whether their email or LinkedIn travels with it.

entries.title: Attend → Posters page now links to a single Poster Gallery and shows its inherited settings
entries.summary: The **Attend → Posters** settings page now uses a single **Poster gallery** picker (with a "No gallery (abstracts only)" option) instead of a multi-select. Once a gallery is chosen, a new **Inherited from \<gallery\>** summary card shows read-only rows for access, embargo, author consent, field visibility, search/filter/grouping, download/share/bookmarks, and content filters — each pulled live from the gallery's own configuration. An **Edit gallery settings** link opens the gallery editor directly. The old screen-title input and standalone embargo card have been removed. A stored gallery that no longer exists on the event shows a blocking warning instead of silently saving a bad ID.
entries.use_case: Events that publish a Poster Gallery no longer need to duplicate embargo and access settings in two places. Organizers pick the gallery once and the Attend Posters page automatically reflects whatever the gallery is configured to show, with a direct link to edit those settings if anything needs changing.

cs_action.note: The old multi-select of galleries and the standalone embargo card are gone. Any event that had multiple galleries selected will now show only the first. Verify with customers who had complex multi-gallery Attend setups before they notice the change.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why their Attend Posters page looks different, or when onboarding an event that uses both Poster Gallery and the Attend app.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Attend beta with at least one Poster Gallery configured on their event.
internal.gotchas: Events with exactly one gallery have it pre-selected on first visit — no action needed. Events with a gallery ID that no longer exists will see a blocking error rather than a silent bad save; advise the organizer to re-select the correct gallery. The PUT payload no longer sends title or embargo fields, but the API before the paired backend release accepts the body without errors.
internal.talk_track: Instead of managing embargo and access in two separate places, you now pick your Poster Gallery once on the Attend Posters page and everything it controls — embargo dates, author consent, search, filters, downloads — is shown right there in a read-only summary with a one-click link to edit it.

entries.title: Enable attendee contact exchange in the Attend app's Networking settings
entries.summary: A new **Contact exchange** toggle in **Attend → Networking** lets organizers enable attendee-to-attendee contact sharing in the mobile app. When on, each attendee controls what they share, and the feature works independently of the attendee directory. A new **Contacts exchanged** stat tile shows the total exchanges and the number of people currently scanning.

enable.path: Attend → Networking → Contact exchange

entries.use_case: Events that want to facilitate in-person networking can let attendees scan and exchange contact details directly in the app, without requiring a public attendee directory. Organizers can track adoption in real time via the Contacts exchanged stat tile.

cs_action.note: The toggle and stat tile only appear once the API version that returns exchange_enabled and exchanges is deployed. Confirm the API release has shipped before pointing customers to this setting.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how attendees can share contact details with each other in the Attend app, or when they want networking engagement metrics.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Attend mobile app (beta) who want peer-to-peer contact sharing without exposing a full attendee directory.
internal.gotchas: The Contact exchange switch and Contacts exchanged tile are hidden until the API returns the corresponding fields — they will not appear on older API versions. Both the UI and API releases must be live before the feature is visible.
internal.talk_track: You can now let attendees exchange contact details by scanning in the app. Each attendee decides what they share, it doesn't require the attendee directory to be on, and you can see how many people are exchanging contacts in real time from the Networking stats panel.

entries.title: Attend Posters now inherit all settings from a single Poster Gallery
entries.summary: The **Attend → Posters** section previously maintained its own duplicate title, embargo rules, and gallery selection. It now reads all configuration — title, fields, search/facets/sort, download/share/bookmark/question switches, author consent, and embargo — directly from one selected **Poster Gallery** (configured under **Publish → Posters**). Changes made in the gallery are immediately reflected in the Attend app without any separate configuration step.
entries.use_case: Events using both a Poster Gallery and the Attend mobile app no longer need to configure embargo rules, field visibility, and display options in two places. Selecting one gallery as the source keeps the app and the web gallery in sync automatically.

cs_action.note: No data migration needed — zero events had Attend poster settings configured in production. Old saved shapes (galleryIds, title, embargo) are read and silently upgraded on the next save.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer uses both Poster Gallery and the Attend app and complains about having to configure embargo or field settings twice.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Attend beta who also use Poster Gallery (beta).
internal.gotchas: The gallery's consent_text is an author-facing statement in the speaker portal; it is not shown to attendees. require_consent filters the poster list to consented posters only, matching the web gallery behaviour. The ME region was not checked for existing data but the migration path is safe regardless.
internal.talk_track: You set up your Poster Gallery once — fields, embargo, download permissions — and the Attend app now picks all of that up automatically. No more keeping two sets of settings in sync.

entries.title: Mobile App editor shows a live, interactive preview of the real app
entries.summary: The canvas in the Mobile App editor now embeds the actual attendee app in an iPhone or Android frame instead of a hand-drawn imitation. Edits stream into the preview instantly — no reload — and the phone is fully clickable: tabs, tiles, session pages, and back navigation all work. A **Use the app / Edit blocks** toggle switches between browsing the app and tapping a block to open its fields in the inspector. Choose **Real data** (your event's published program) or **Sample data** (a generated 3-day program) from the device toolbar. Additional controls let you switch between iPhone and Android frames, light and dark mode, **100% / 200%** text size, display language (English, German, Spanish, French, Arabic/RTL), and reload the preview; settings are remembered per browser. The left rail and the phone stay in sync: picking a page in the rail navigates the phone, and tapping a tab on the phone updates the rail. Events with no published content open automatically on sample data with an explanatory note. The **Unsaved** indicator appears in the rail whenever Access settings have pending changes that require **Save**.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the preview host; then Event → Mobile App → Editor

entries.use_case: Organizers designing their attendee app can see exactly how every layout change will look and behave on a real device — including live navigation, dark mode, and RTL languages — without leaving the editor or needing a simulator.

cs_action.note: The live preview requires VITE_ATTEND_PREVIEW_URL to be set in Doppler and the preview build to be hosted (Cloudflare Pages per sessionboard-mobile docs/live-preview-hosting.md). Until the host is live, the editor falls back to the old drawn canvas automatically — no customer-visible breakage. Pairs with sessionboard-mobile PR #53 and web-api PR #4565 (needed for Real data; Sample data works without it).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the Mobile App (Attend beta) asks how to preview their app design or reports that the canvas doesn't match what attendees see.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Attend Mobile App beta who are actively configuring their app layout with Expo, Pulse, or Mosaic packs.
internal.gotchas: Real data requires web-api #4565 and a published program; events with nothing published open on Sample data automatically. The org-level Mobile App editor (OrgPhonePreview) still uses the old drawn canvas — this improvement is event-scoped only for now. The preview is read-only: no saves, analytics, impressions, check-ins, or push notifications are triggered.
internal.talk_track: Instead of guessing how your app will look, you can now click through the real app right inside the editor — switch packs, change a block, and see it update live in an iPhone or Android frame. You can even test dark mode, large text, and Arabic RTL before your event goes live.

entries.title: Mobile App settings move to Attend → Overview; Networking gets a handshake icon
entries.summary: **Mobile App** (attendee app design, sign-in, push notifications, and profile settings) has moved from the Publish section of the sidebar into **Attend → Overview**. The **Networking** item now displays a handshake icon instead of the network icon.
entries.use_case: Organizers configuring the attendee mobile app no longer need to look under Publish — all app settings are grouped with the rest of the Attend experience, making it faster to find and configure the app alongside other attendee-facing features.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer cannot find Mobile App settings and is looking under Publish.
